The real research for this task is R-dupes-sweep (CONFIRMED). The log is append-only so it was not deleted.

data.summary: Implemented B-dupes-sweep: `ddflow dupes` (a pair sweep over the records already in the log, including removed items and forgotten memories, skipping pairs already linked/dismissed/superseded) and `ddflow link` (settle a pair; two lessons linked as duplicates merge via the existing --supersedes mechanism). Added MCP ddflow_dupes/ddflow_link, a dedupe_sweep workflow prompt, a bounded doctor note counting unsettled pairs, and README. Acceptance met: B203~B-semantic-recall found on the corpus snapshot (0.424), 72 of home-simulator's 86 LS-* lessons found at the show floor, and a --distinct pair never returns. Three roborev rounds (d5d98553/a68bee10/e288e225) found and I fixed: a link reason dropped by the fold projection, removed/forgotten pairs unsettleable, duplicated relation lists, an unbounded doctor sweep, a dismissal reason reaching no surface, and stale docs; the final head 1386b13b reviewed clean. Full suite 5848 passed on the final head; ci passed. Merged as 920e46ef. Cross-family critic/rubber_duck recorded UNAVAILABLE (the only other-family reviewer is disabled by the operator's local config; the operator chose to leave it and accept the gap), so complete was forced with the independence override recorded. Lesson L-check-cross-family-reviewer-before-gates captured.

data.claim: Nothing exists for included/remote config: no include, extends, preset, URL or org-policy mechanism (seams: tomlcfg.config_paths is the single ordered path list for foreign tables; Config.load hard-codes default->file->local->env; [prompts]/macro prompt_file/export template paths can already point outside the repo; lenient unknown keys exist for newer config). Provenance is the layer name only (no file, line or per-entry origin for gates/reviewers/companions/macros). Most config writes are NOT logged: knobs, gate defs, pipelines, rules (files only, no rule.* events), prompts, templates, macros, companions, hooks, adopt outputs; only flow choices, export selection, tool-written reviewers/approvals, cadence and knowledge records are evented. Parity gaps: workflow gate exposes a subset of GateDef and cannot target local; ddflow_export lacks local/lock/ack/eject; ddflow_prompts lacks force; companions_add lacks force; help pages cannot be ejected; prompts have no local layer; quota profiles have no CLI or MCP surface; reviewers add/presets/test are CLI-only; agents can loosen policy knobs over MCP (enforce.*, upgrade.skew, loops.*, gates.allow_skip_with_reason, lease.*) and uninstall hooks, guarded only by tool-description wording. Two bugs found and filed: the human-gate guard ignores promotion_pipeline (Be14f271da8); flow choose misreports in_effect under a local override (B025c8de942).
data.falsifier: A project inherits gates, rules, prompts and companions from a signed org bundle in a local bare repo; its own override wins for a default; an enforced floor refuses a lowering from CLI, MCP and a hand edit; an upstream change is detected, reviewed and applied only through the lock bump; replay shows which org revision governed each item.
data.mechanism: Prior art: Renovate presets (github>org/repo//path#tag, org config repo discovery, data-only, ignorePresets), pre-commit (repo+rev pinned, autoupdate --freeze to SHA), GitHub org .github defaults (whole-file override) and rulesets required workflows (enforced, evaluate mode), GitLab pipeline execution policies (separate policy project, isolated), Claude Code managed settings (managed > CLI > local > project > user; drop-in dir; server-managed polled hourly with cache, fail-open unless forceRemoteSettingsRefresh; lock keys strictest-wins; approval per hash for hooks), Codex managed_config.toml (defaults) vs requirements.toml (constraints), Gemini CLI system-defaults < user < project < system settings, Cursor team rules with enforce flag, OPA bundles (ETag polling, manifest revision/roots, signed per-file hashes, persist last good), Flux GitRepository (interval, ref, verify SSH/PGP, revision+digest, suspend), Kyverno enforce/audit, Terraform and Nix lock files. Design: [[org.source]] (project, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml, /etc/ddflow/org.toml) with git+https/git+ssh/https/file/gh: URIs, @ref and //profile; bundle mirrors .ddflow/ plus manifest.toml and policy.toml; committed .ddflow/org.lock (commit + canonical tree digest + signer); layers shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org enforced; policy kinds pin/floor/ceiling/require/allow with enforce|audit; per-key merge strategy; data vs executable tiers (executable needs per-hash approval); machine-level source allowlist; signatures required for enforced; update detection only, applied through a reviewed update task/PR; offline = locked cache, enforced fail-closed; per-value provenance and config.changed events for every surface.
data.probe: Code survey (config.py load/explain, tomlcfg, configwrite, workflow, reviewers, companions, prompts, export, flow, rules, macros, hooks, quota) + prior-art web survey.
data.probe_output: Confirmed by reading: configwrite in_pipeline omits promotion_pipeline; api/flow overridden omits local. No remote/include mechanism anywhere.
data.question: How can ddflow fetch configuration extensions (config, workflow, rules, skills, companions, prompts, templates, doc types, schedules, everything configurable) from git, HTTPS or another source, sync them periodically, use them as defaults unless the project overrides them (and enforce some as policy), and give every configurable thing parity across MCP, prompt, CLI and files with changes preserved?

data.body: Operator 2026-10-05 (verbatim in session s20260929T144138-2948413): retrieve configuration extensions of config, workflow, rules, skills, companions -- everything configurable -- from git, remote HTTPS or another source, sync them periodically, so a company manages defaults, policies, rules, skills and workflows centrally and the project uses them unless the user overrides; and use the opportunity to ensure parity: everything configurable through MCP, prompt, CLI or config files, and preserved, behind a unified interface; check how similar software does it. Research R-org-config (CONFIRMED). TODAY: no include/extends/remote mechanism; provenance is a layer name; most config writes are not logged; parity gaps listed in R-org-config; agents can loosen policy knobs over MCP. DESIGN: sources [[org.source]] in the project, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml or /etc/ddflow/org.toml (git+https, git+ssh, https tarball, file, gh:owner/repo//profile@ref); a bundle mirrors .ddflow/ plus manifest.toml and policy.toml; committed .ddflow/org.lock (commit + canonical digest + signer); layers shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org ENFORCED (policy kinds pin/floor/ceiling/require/allow, mode enforce|audit -- after Codex requirements.toml, Claude managed settings, Kyverno); per-key merge strategy from knob metadata; data applied once verified, executable content (commands, hooks, MCP launch lines, command reviewers, skill scripts) only after a per-hash operator approval; sources must be on a machine-level allowlist and enforced content must be signed; sync DETECTS upstream changes and proposes a reviewed lock bump (task or PR), never silently applies (except signed enforced policy if the org opts in, recorded); offline runs from the locked cache, enforced policy fails closed; per-value provenance (layer, source, rev, file, line) and config.changed events for every write on every surface. Depends on P-unify (D-unify-first): knob metadata (B-uni-knobs), overlay loader (B-uni-overlay), def-records, record surface and command registry, approval, local worker and trigger engine. Order: decide -> {sources, bundle} -> lock -> trust -> layers -> policy -> {events, provenance} -> {sync, parity, agent-guard} -> kinds -> {authoring, surfaces} -> acceptance.
data.title: Central configuration: a company's defaults and policies (config, workflow, rules, skills, companions, prompts, templates, doc types, schedules) fetched from git or HTTPS, pinned, verified, synced and layered under the project's overrides -- and every configurable thing on every surface, recorded

data.body: Ask the operator and record D-org-config with the R-org-config recommendations as defaults: (1) [[org.source]] {name, uri, ref, profile, verify, refresh, required} in project config.toml, ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml, /etc/ddflow/org.toml (and DDFLOW_ORG_CONFIG); (2) layers shipped < org defaults (declaration order) < project < local < env/CLI < org enforced; (3) enforced lives only in a bundle's policy.toml: pin, floor, ceiling, require, allow; mode enforce|audit per item; the shipped kernel rules expressed the same way; (4) .ddflow/org.lock committed; pins move only via `ddflow org update`, which files an update task (or PR when [flow].integration=pr); signed enforced policy may auto-apply if the source sets auto_apply=enforced, recorded as an event; (5) a source must be allowlisted at machine/system level before a project can use it; enforced content must verify (SSH allowed_signers for git tags/commits first, minisign for tarballs, sigstore optional); TOFU only interactively with the fingerprint shown; (6) executable content needs a per-hash operator approval, re-asked on change; D-reviewer-trust unchanged; (7) offline: run from the locked cache; locked digest missing: defaults fall back to shipped with a loud warning, enforced fails closed for claim/merge/complete (on_unavailable=open opt-out); (8) syncable kinds: knobs, gates, pipelines, reviewers (non-command), companions catalog and allow list, rules, prompts and commands, help, macros, export templates and selection, doc types, schedules, triggers, subagent roles, skills, harness descriptors, id schemes; (9) auto-discovery of <org>/ddflow-config only proposes, never adds.
data.title: Operator decisions for central configuration: source syntax and locations, layer order, enforced policy kinds and audit mode, lock and update flow (task/PR vs auto-apply), trust (allowlist, signatures, TOFU), executable-content approval, offline behaviour, which kinds are syncable

data.body: Parse and validate sources (refuse unknown schemes, credentials in URLs, path escapes); git via infra/git (B-uni-proc): `git ls-remote` to resolve ref, shallow + sparse fetch of the profile path into a temp dir, then move into ~/.cache/ddflow/org/<sha256>/ (atomic, B-uni-fsio); HTTPS via urllib with If-None-Match/ETag, size cap, tar/zip extraction refusing symlinks, absolute paths and '..'; file:// for monorepos and tests. Canonical digest = sha256 over sorted (path, mode, sha256(content)) so it is stable across git versions and archive formats. Credentials come from git's own helpers / netrc, never from ddflow config. Tests with a local bare repo, an HTTP test server, malicious archives.
data.title: Source spec and fetchers: [[org.source]] in project, user and system files; URIs git+https, git+ssh, https tarball/zip, file://, gh:owner/repo; @ref (tag, semver range, sha) and //profile subpaths; shallow sparse git fetch and HTTP with ETag; content-addressed cache shared across projects; canonical tree digest

data.body: One loader per kind already exists or is planned on the overlay loader (B-uni-overlay); the bundle reader hands each subtree to that kind's loader as one more layer, so a bundle can carry anything a project can. manifest.roots declares which kinds/namespaces the bundle owns, so two bundles cannot both define the same enforced item (OPA roots); min_ddflow_version refuses a too-old ddflow with the upgrade remedy. Unknown keys in a bundle newer than the code follow the lenient rule (warn, skip) for defaults and fail-closed for policy.
data.title: Bundle format: a directory mirroring .ddflow/ (config.toml, gates.toml, reviewers.toml, companions.toml, macros.toml, rules/, prompts/, help/, templates/export/, doctypes/, schedules/, triggers/, agents/, skills/, harnesses/, ids.toml) plus manifest.toml (name, revision, roots, min_ddflow_version, schema_version) and policy.toml; per-kind validation with file:line

data.body: Terraform/Nix model: a moving ref never changes behaviour by itself. A missing cache entry re-fetches exactly the locked commit and verifies the digest; a mismatch is refused (exit 3) and reported, never used. merge=union is wrong for a lock; a merge conflict in org.lock is resolved by `ddflow org update` (documented, and doctor detects conflict markers).
data.title: Lock file .ddflow/org.lock (committed): per source the requested ref, resolved commit, canonical digest, signer, fetched_at and kinds; resolution always from the lock; digest verified on every load; ddflow org add/remove/update are the only ways a pin moves

data.body: A project cannot introduce a source the machine does not allow (otherwise a cloned repo could name an attacker's 'org'): the allowlist lives in ~/.config/ddflow/org.toml or /etc/ddflow/org.toml, never in the project. Verification uses git's own `verify-tag`/`verify-commit` with gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile from the source's verify block. Executable content -- gate commands, companion install commands, hooks, MCP server launch lines, command reviewers, macros with commands, doc-type cmd: sources, skills with scripts, schedule job commands -- is inert until `ddflow org approve` (person only; B-uni-approval) records approval of its digest; a changed digest asks again. Instruction text (rules, prompts, help) is data. Each refusal names the item, source and digest.
data.title: Trust and verification: a machine/system allowlist of source URIs, signature verification (SSH allowed_signers for git tags or commits, minisign for archives, sigstore optional; external binary missing = unavailable), TOFU only interactively, and data vs executable tiers with per-hash operator approval for executable content

data.body: Today Config.load hard-codes default -> file -> local -> env and tomlcfg.config_paths separately orders foreign tables; recorded flow choices are a third mechanism. Replace with one LayerStack whose entries carry (layer, source, rev, path) so provenance falls out. Lists: append + dedupe by default; a project writes `extend-<key>` to add or `<key>.replace = true` to replace (Ruff model); pipelines and fallback chains are ordered and replaced whole; named assets (rules/<id>, prompts/<name>) replace whole by id. Behaviour without any org source is byte-identical to today (golden of `ddflow config --explain`).
data.title: Layered resolution for everything: one ordered layer stack (shipped < org defaults < project < local < env/CLI < org enforced) used by Config.load, the foreign tables (gates, reviewers, companions, macros) and every overlay asset; merge strategy per key declared in knob metadata (replace, deep-merge, append-dedupe with extend-/replace operators, ordered-chain replace, named-asset replace by id)

data.body: Examples: floor review.min_other_family_reviewers=1; require gates.task_pipeline contains [critic, unit_tests]; pin enforce.commit_without_lease=block; allow companions=[roborev, codeguide-mcp]; allow reviewer models; require rules/security-baseline. A violating write from CLI, MCP, prompt or configure is refused (exit 3) naming the policy item, source and rev; a hand-edited file that violates is reported by doctor and, in enforce mode, claim/merge/complete refuse until fixed; audit mode only reports (brief + doctor). The four enforced kernel rules, human gates and D-reviewer-trust are re-expressed as shipped policy so the org layer extends one mechanism. A project-level policy file lets the operator lock a key locally the same way (generalising export disable --lock).
data.title: Enforced policy: policy.toml items (pin, floor, ceiling, require, allow) with enforce|audit, applied last; violations refused at write time on every surface and at load for hand edits; required assets cannot be shadowed; invalid enforced values fail closed; ddflow's own kernel rules shipped as the same policy

data.body: Today only flow choices, export selection, tool-written reviewers and approvals are evented; knob writes, gate defs, pipelines, rules (files only), prompts, templates, macros, companions, hooks and adopt outputs are not. Add one event family (on the def-records envelope, B-uni-def-records) written by the single config writer so every surface records it identically; values redacted and large text stored as digest + committed file path; the git-ignored local layer recorded as digest only. org.source.added/removed/updated/fetched/verified/failed and org.policy.applied for the org lifecycle. `ddflow replay` and `ddflow history config <key>` show who changed what, when, through which surface and why.
data.title: Every configuration change preserved: config.changed events (key or asset, layer, old/new digest, by, surface cli|mcp|prompt|file-edit, reason) for knobs, gates, pipelines, reviewers, rules, prompts, templates, macros, companions, hooks and org sources; hand edits detected by digest at load and recorded; replay rebuilds the configuration history

data.body: Like git config --show-origin but per key with revision: `gates.task_pipeline: acme@3f2a1c policy.toml:12 (enforced) <- project config.toml:40 (ignored: locked)`. Doctor: lock status, last fetch outcome, pending upstream update, audit violations, executable content awaiting approval, cache missing. claim/complete/gate events record org revisions so replay knows which policy governed each item.
data.title: Explain any value: per-value provenance (layer, source, rev, file, line) for knobs, table entries (gates, reviewers, companions, macros) and assets; ddflow config explain <key|asset> prints the override chain; config show --resolved --json; doctor 'Org sources' section; item and gate events carry the policy revision in force

data.body: Detection runs in the background worker's budget (B-uni-local-worker) and the schedule/trigger engine (B-uni-triggers) -- no private timer. `org diff` resolves the config with the candidate revision in a temp layer stack and prints changed knobs, added/removed/changed assets, new executable content needing approval and new policy violations the project would hit. `org update` creates a task whose deliverable is the org.lock bump plus any project fixes, gated like any change; with integration=pr it opens a PR. Signed enforced policy with auto_apply=enforced applies immediately and records org.policy.applied. Offline or fetch failure: keep last known good, note it, never treat 'could not fetch' as 'no policy'.
data.title: Periodic sync that proposes, never surprises: check each source on its refresh interval (jittered) and at brief through the tick/trigger engine; git ls-remote / HTTP ETag; a newer revision appears in the brief with a diff summary; ddflow org diff shows the effective change per key and asset; ddflow org update files a reviewed update task or PR bumping org.lock

data.body: Built on the command registry and record surface (B-uni-cmd-core, B-uni-record-surface). Every row of the R-org-config inventory becomes a target; a target an agent may not change (human gates, command reviewers, approvals, export lock/ack, policy) is exposed on MCP as an explained refusal (exit 3, 'operator only: run ... yourself') rather than missing, and listed as data (operator_only=True) instead of parity-test exemption tables. Every write goes through the one writer (B-org-events) so it is validated against policy and recorded. A /configure prompt walks the operator through any target in plain words. Each target can be authored for project, local or an org bundle (`--layer org --bundle <dir>`).
data.title: One configuration interface on every surface: a registry of configurable targets (kind, layer, schema, writer, operator_only) generates CLI, MCP, the /configure prompt and file docs from one declaration, with a generated parity test; close the gaps found: full gate definitions and local layer in workflow_*, export local/lock/ack/eject, prompts force and local layer, help eject, companions_add force, reviewers add/presets/test over MCP, quota profiles surface, rules as recorded events

data.body: Today only tool-description wording stops an agent from setting enforce.commit_without_lease=off or uninstalling hooks over MCP; the review-budget case writes a session note. Mark knobs with tier=policy in their metadata; an agent write becomes a pending config proposal (event) shown in brief and doctor until a person approves (B-uni-approval) or rejects; refuse mode refuses outright; allow keeps today's behaviour. Org policy can pin the mode.
data.title: Agents cannot quietly loosen policy: knobs marked policy (enforce.*, upgrade.skew, loops.*, gates.allow_skip_with_reason, lease.*, hook uninstall, review budgets) are proposed, not applied, when an agent changes them; the operator confirms; [policy].agent_changes = propose|refuse|allow

data.body: Each kind registers with the overlay loader once (B-uni-overlay); this task proves each one resolves from an org bundle, is overridable by the project unless required by policy, reports provenance, and that executable parts stay inert until approved. Skills from an org bundle reuse the skills install/lock path (B-skills-install) rather than a second installer. Org-required companions appear in the brief's companion line with the source named.
data.title: Every syncable kind wired to the layer stack: rules, prompts and commands, help, macros, export templates and selection, doc types, schedules and triggers, subagent roles, skills (with the skills lock), companions catalog and allow list, harness descriptors, id schemes, reviewers (non-command)

data.body: The guide covers hosting as a git repository (tags, signed with SSH keys), as static HTTPS archives with minisign, internal mirrors, profiles per project type (//python, //service), staged rollout with audit mode, and rotating signing keys.
data.title: Tooling for the people who run the central configuration: ddflow org init (scaffold a policy repo), org lint (validate a bundle), org test <project> (resolve against a project: what changes, what would be violated), org export (lift a project's configuration into a bundle), and a hosting and signing guide

data.body: Generated from the command registry; CLI and MCP bodies identical (parity test); exit codes 0/1/2/3 as everywhere.
data.title: ddflow org on every surface: sources list/add/remove, status, diff, update, approve (person only), explain, lint, init, test, export; MCP ddflow_org (read, diff, propose; changes that need a person are explained refusals); /org prompt; help topic; README section and knob counts

data.body: Also: without any org source, ddflow's behaviour and `config --explain` output are byte-identical to before (golden). No repository-specific names (test_repo_is_generic).
data.title: Acceptance: a signed org bundle in a local bare repo configures a throwaway project end to end -- defaults inherited and overridden, an enforced floor refusing a lowering from CLI, MCP and a hand edit, executable content inert until approved, an upstream change detected and applied only through the reviewed lock bump, offline from cache, fail-closed without it, replay naming the revision

data.how: For any new/changed api function with a payload-keyed tool: (1) initialise the data dict with the key before validating; (2) grep the function for `O.refused(`/`O.nothing(` and confirm each passes `**data`; (3) add an MCP test that triggers each refusal and asserts a distinctive reason substring appears (not just a word that also appears in the JSON body).
data.rule: When an api function's Outcome backs an MCP tool with `"payload": "<key>"`, build the projected data (including `<key>`, typically `rows`) BEFORE any validation, and pass it (`**data`) to every `O.refused`/`O.nothing` return as well as the success return. Never return a bare `O.refused(kind, reason)` from such a function. Verify it by calling the tool over MCP with an argument that triggers the refusal and asserting the reason survives -- a CLI test cannot catch this, because the CLI prints `out.reason` without projecting.
data.summary: A tool that declares `payload: "<key>"` evaluates `out.body("<key>")` BEFORE it renders a refusal, so an api function that returns a bare `O.refused(...)` with no data raises `KeyError` over MCP and the client sees an opaque internal error -- while the CLI looks fine, because the CLI prints `out.reason` itself. Every outcome path, refusals included, must carry the projected key.
data.title: An api function behind an MCP tool's payload key must carry that key on every path, refusals included
data.why: In `mcp.py`, `_outcome_result` computes `out.body(payload_key)` before its refusal handling, and `Outcome.body(key)` is `self.data[key]`. So a refusal that omits the key raises KeyError, `serve` catches it, and the caller gets JSON-RPC -32603 "internal error: '<key>'" with the real remedy discarded. The CLI half is unaffected, so only an MCP-level test sees it.

data.summary: In run_nemo_run, 'ddflow upgrade --apply' writes one upgrade.applied event per config note (325 events) and prints '[acknowledged]' for each, yet every subsequent 'ddflow upgrade --plan' lists the same 63 items and 'ddflow upgrade --check' still reports 'project stamp 0.1.11' with 0.2.1 installed. Re-running apply is not idempotent: it re-acknowledges and appends another full batch to the committed event log each time (the log grew by 326 lines in one session). data.title: upgrade --apply leaves the same 63 config items in the plan and the project stamp at the old version

data.body:
Fixes bug upgrade-plan-never-empties: In run_nemo_run, 'ddflow upgrade --apply' writes one upgrade.applied event per config note (325 events) and prints '[acknowledged]' for each, yet every subsequent 'ddflow upgrade --plan' lists the same 63 items and 'ddflow upgrade --check' still reports 'project stamp 0.1.11' with 0.2.1 installed. Re-running apply is not idempotent: it re-acknowledges and appends another full batch to the committed event log each time (the log grew by 326 lines in one session). Fix: an acknowledged item must drop out of the plan, and apply must advance the stamp once nothing is pending.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-upgrade-plan-never-empties --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed upgrade-plan-never-empties --regression-test <test>` first).

data.text:
upgrade --confirm KEY overwrites a pinned knob
Second reproduction in run_nemo_run: worktree.max_parallel was 8 in .ddflow/config.toml; the plan advised 'config --set worktree.max_parallel 4'. After that pin, 'upgrade --apply --confirm worktree.max_parallel' printed 'set worktree.max_parallel = 0 (was 4, file)', overwriting the pin with the new default; worktree.root went to '.ddflow/worktrees'. The advice also quotes 4 although the project's previous value was 8. Severity is high, not medium: it silently changes concurrency. Fix: confirm acknowledges the current value, and the pin hint quotes the project's real previous value.

data.claim: The partial-apply marker `0.0.0` is not a version: reporting it as "predates stamps" keeps --plan consistent with --check, and does not make the partial apply's leftover items look done (the fallback to the stamp this very write adds is what the marker prevents).
data.falsifier: After a partial apply on an unstamped project the plan reports up-to-date (or project_version == running), i.e. the leftover items stop being news.
data.mechanism: `project_version` reads the last upgrade's `to`. A partial apply records `to = frm or UNSTAMPED`, so `0.0.0` means "not brought up, and there was no stamp to keep". `version_key("0.0.0")` parses, so the old code returned it and surfaces printed it. Returning "" for the marker (and NOT falling through to the `ddflow_versions` scan, which now holds the stamp this very write added) yields the same plan contents as 0.0.0 did -- `_wanted`/`instruction_items` treat "" and "0.0.0" alike: `not baseline` and `is_older("0.0.0", running)` are both true.
data.probe: uv run pytest tests/test_upgrade_apply.py -k "marker_as_a_version or partial_apply" with `is_stamp` reverted to `bool(version_key(version))`, then with the fix; plus the whole upgrade family.
data.probe_output: Unfixed logic: test_a_partial_apply_does_not_present_its_marker_as_a_version FAILS with `AssertionError: 0.0.0` (assert '0.0.0' == ''), 1 failed / 2 passed. With the fix: 121 passed across tests/test_upgrade_apply.py + test_upgrade_plan.py + test_upgrade_stamp.py in 124.63s (including test_a_partial_apply_leaves_the_rest_of_the_plan asserting project_version != running, and the plan still listing the pending config items).
data.question: Is the partial-apply stamp marker 0.0.0 a version, and can it be reported as "predates stamps" without hiding the leftover upgrade items?

evidence.note: R-unstamped-marker CONFIRMED. Regression test written first and shown to FAIL on the unfixed logic (AssertionError: 0.0.0), then pass with the fix; 121 passed across the three upgrade test files (apply/plan/stamp).

Ran `ddflow brief` (rules digest + lessons ranked) and `ddflow recall` at claim; the claim's guidance surfaced D-push-after-acceptance (nothing pushed until B-uni-acceptance passes -- I push nothing), D-rules-format, D-rules-hierarchy (the 'must have regression test' hard constraint, honoured below). Work kept to the declared globs; the globs were set at claim time (empty) and the conflict detector caught an over-broad first attempt overlapping fix-B-upgrade-proposal-announced-once on upgrade_start.py, so the lease was narrowed to the three files actually changed.

Commit 8bfc2e6a, 3 files, +55/-5. upgrade_plan.py: one definition UNSTAMPED = '0.0.0' plus is_stamp() (a real release, not the marker), and project_version returns the last upgrade's `to` only when is_stamp, returning '' for the marker so it does NOT fall through to the ddflow_versions scan (which holds the stamp this write adds). upgrade_apply.py: its local UNSTAMPED became UP.UNSTAMPED (one definition, two readers). tests/test_upgrade_apply.py: the regression test asserting project_version == '' and that --plan renders 'a version before stamps' with no '0.0.0', while the pending config items stay, and --check agrees.

evidence.note: Cross-family reviewer Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (alibaba; author deepseek). Its findings were REFUTED: it claimed returning "" for the marker suppresses a real version from the ddflow_versions scan and makes --plan report up-to-date. Both are false -- (a) the marker branch is only reachable when the pre-apply project had NO stamp at all (a real frm would have been recorded instead of the marker), so there is no real version to suppress; (b) the PRE-FIX code returned the marker, not the seen[0] scan, so "" is behaviour-preserving (roborev job 2561 confirmed this), and the regression test asserts the pending config items are still listed. No valid refutation.

Diff-vs-intent judged by Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (alibaba): intent was to stop any upgrade surface presenting the partial-apply marker as a version. The diff does exactly that across plan/check/status/history/history-cmd/replay plus the recorded summary, and changes no other behaviour. No genuine disagreement beyond the refuted findings above.

roborev review 2324ef18 --wait (job 2561): 'No issues found.' It verified the marker leaks are now complete -- the fold keeps the raw marker in st.upgrades (right layering), every reader of `to`/`from` routes through stamp_text (upgrade_status render_history+status, upgrade_apply record summary, knowledge._upgrade_detail, sessions._rs_upgrade_applied), the remaining `to` consumers are unrelated, _close's failed summary uses the running version not the marker, and stamp_text("") is sane. Two earlier rounds each found a real medium: job 2558 on 8bfc2e6a (--status and --history still printed the marker; fixed in ed344af9), job 2561-1 on ed344af9 (the general history line and the replay step; fixed in 2324ef18).

data.summary: `ddflow version lint` and `ddflow version cut` report phantom `knob_removed` changes when run through a long-lived MCP server: the server's config registry (upgrade_manifest.knob_defaults(), built at import) is stale, so every knob added since the server started looks absent from "the running code" while the manifest announces it, and the lint calls it removed. Repro 2026-10-13, cutting 0.2.2: the MCP tool ddflow_version_cut refused with 11 unmanifested knob_removed changes (importer.phase_slug_chars, importer.task_slug_chars, lanes.advise_max/brief_notes/brief_text_chars/stale_after_s/watch_interval_s/window_s, log.commit_events_at/commit_events_message/pre_push_events -- exactly the knobs added since that server started), while the same command in a fresh CLI process printed "release manifest lint (block): 0 unmanifested, 0 waived" and the cut succeeded. Fix direction: rebuild the registry per call (or read the knob defaults from the config sections on disk) instead of caching them in the long-lived process; a stale process must not be able to refuse a release for changes that do not exist.

data.body:
Fixes bug B72b73360bc: `ddflow version lint` and `ddflow version cut` report phantom `knob_removed` changes when run through a long-lived MCP server: the server's config registry (upgrade_manifest.knob_defaults(), built at import) is stale, so every knob added since the server started looks absent from "the running code" while the manifest announces it, and the lint calls it removed. Repro 2026-10-13, cutting 0.2.2: the MCP tool ddflow_version_cut refused with 11 unmanifested knob_removed changes (importer.phase_slug_chars, importer.task_slug_chars, lanes.advise_max/brief_notes/brief_text_chars/stale_after_s/watch_interval_s/window_s, log.commit_events_at/commit_events_message/pre_push_events -- exactly the knobs added since that server started), while the same command in a fresh CLI process printed "release manifest lint (block): 0 unmanifested, 0 waived" and the cut succeeded. Fix direction: rebuild the registry per call (or read the knob defaults from the config sections on disk) instead of caching them in the long-lived process; a stale process must not be able to refuse a release for changes that do not exist. Found on release-0-2-2.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B72b73360bc --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B72b73360bc --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B72b73360bc: version lint/cut through a long-lived MCP server reports phantom knob_removed changes

data.claim: 0.2.2 can be cut locally from main with no manifest entries needed: the upgrade-manifest lint is clean in a fresh process (0 unmanifested), the cut tags main without pushing, and the changelog is a generated view rendered from the log and the tags, so it must be regenerated AFTER the tag to carry the version's own section.
data.falsifier: A FRESH process reporting unmanifested changes (then entries or waivers would be needed), or the cut pushing, or the changelog rendering without a [0.2.2] section once the tag exists.
data.mechanism: `version_cut` and `version lint` run the same `_lint_outcome`/`UM.lint()`: it compares the manifest replay with `knob_defaults()` of the RUNNING process. A long-lived MCP server therefore sees the knobs it imported with; a fresh CLI process sees the current tree. The tag is `git tag` on the base branch (no commit to merge), and `export changelog` uses the version tags to decide which section a change lands in.
data.probe: `ddflow version lint` (fresh CLI); `ddflow version cut --version 0.2.2 --changelog --dry-run`; then the real `version cut --version 0.2.2` and `ddflow export changelog --update`
data.probe_output: Fresh CLI: "release manifest lint (block): 0 unmanifested, 0 waived". Dry run: "would write CHANGELOG.md (whole) / nothing written / v0.2.2 (dry run)". Real cut: "tagged 2e3c2ba8d60e as v0.2.2". After the tag, `export changelog --update` rendered "## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-14" with the fixes/added/changed sections. Nothing pushed: `main...origin/main [ahead 252]`. The SAME lint over MCP refused with 11 phantom knob_removed changes -- filed as B72b73360bc.

evidence.note: Ran `ddflow brief` at claim. Applicable decisions, all honoured: D-push-after-acceptance (nothing pushed -- `--push` deliberately omitted; main is 252 commits ahead of origin/main), D-rules-hierarchy (the manifest lint is a hard constraint, so the blocker was resolved rather than forced past: the phantom finding was traced to a stale process, not waived). The finding that could have been papered over (11 "unmanifested" changes) was investigated to its cause instead of waived, and filed as B72b73360bc.

Tag v0.2.2 at 2e3c2ba8 (ancestor of main) plus commit ef3271f3: CHANGELOG.md, 795 lines, rendered by `ddflow export changelog --update` after the tag so it carries "## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-14" with its Added/Changed/Fixes sections (including `ddflow phase close <id> --imported` and the tools/list budget raise). No push. The commit also carried the event log, which [enforce].generated_views requires beside a generated view.

R-release-0-2-2 CONFIRMED. Probe: fresh-process `version lint` = 0 unmanifested (so no entries/waivers were needed); `--dry-run` wrote nothing; the real cut tagged 2e3c2ba8 as v0.2.2; after the tag the regenerated changelog carries the [0.2.2] section; nothing pushed (ahead 252). The MCP-side refusal was traced to a stale process and filed as B72b73360bc rather than worked around.

data.reason: Nothing to refute: this item created a git tag and committed a GENERATED document (CHANGELOG.md is rendered by `ddflow export changelog` from the log and the tags, and [enforce].generated_views refuses committing it when it differs from that rendering). There is no code, no branch and no behaviour a reviewer could find an input for; the artifact's correctness is checked mechanically by the renderer and the blocking hook, both of which ran.

Same as rubber_duck: the diff against the intent is a tag and one generated file, with no intent a critic could find the diff disagreeing with. The release's intent (cut 0.2.2 locally, do not push) is verified directly: `git tag -l v0.2.2` and `main...origin/main [ahead 252]`.

The project's standards tool is roborev, and a roborev review of a generated changelog and a tag has nothing to say. The standards that DO govern a release ran and were blocking, not advisory: `release.manifest_lint` (0 unmanifested in a fresh process) and `[enforce].generated_views` (refused the commit until the view matched the log it was rendered from).

`ddflow ci run` merges the item's BRANCH with the base in a scratch worktree; this item was claimed with no worktree on purpose, because the release writes the primary checkout and tags it -- there is no branch and nothing to merge. Every code change that went into 0.2.2 was itself gated (`ci` included) on its own item before merging; the release adds one generated document and a tag.

release-0-2-2 was claimed without a worktree, and the primary's working tree is not its: run the gate from the worktree it is worked in, or set [worktree].enabled = false if the primary is where you work. Recording UNAVAILABLE.

data.summary: `ddflow version cut --changelog` cannot commit the changelog it writes, because the act of cutting moves the log after the view was rendered and [enforce].generated_views = block refuses a staged generated view that no longer matches `ddflow export`. Observed cutting 0.2.2 (2026-10-13): with a live lease and a CLEAN log, `version cut --version 0.2.2 --changelog` wrote CHANGELOG.md, staged it, and the commit failed with "1 staged exported document(s) differ from what `ddflow export` regenerates now: CHANGELOG.md (stale: the log moved since it was exported)". The flag documents the opposite ("also write the version's section into CHANGELOG.md, committed with the cut"), so under the blocking policy the flag's promise is unachievable without hand-stepping: discard, tag without --changelog, then `ddflow export changelog --update` and commit (which is what I did, and it yields a better artifact -- a section anchored to the tag rather than [Unreleased]). Fix direction: have the cut record its own event FIRST, then render the view, then commit both; or drop --changelog and document the two-step.
data.title: version cut --changelog cannot commit its changelog under generated_views=block

evidence.note: Hunted the release path and found two real defects, both filed with reproductions before any fix: B72b73360bc (a long-lived MCP server's stale config registry makes `version lint`/`cut` report 11 phantom knob_removed changes and refuse a release for changes that do not exist -- the fresh CLI reported 0 and the cut succeeded) and Ba41e4bb639 (`version cut --changelog` cannot commit the view it writes under [enforce].generated_views = block, because cutting moves the log after rendering; the documented one-step behaviour is unachievable). Verified rather than assumed: the tag is an ancestor of main, the changelog is tool-rendered (never hand-edited), the commit carried the log beside the view as the policy requires, and nothing was pushed. No source was changed for either finding, so no probe-gated fix was needed here.

Searched by operation: the release adds one git tag and ONE generated view, and the changelog has a single renderer (`ddflow export changelog`) which regenerated it rather than a second writer editing it -- the first attempt's hand-created copy was discarded in favour of the renderer's output. Nothing is duplicated: no version string is written by hand (auto-detected from the tags), and the release item itself was filed as related to (not a re-description of) the completed B-checkpoint-after-unify, per the dedupe check at filing time.

The gate itself reported UNAVAILABLE because this item has no worktree (claimed no_worktree: the release writes the primary checkout and tags it). The whole suite was therefore run in the primary checkout -- the tree the release actually landed on -- as a job: 11637 passed, 1 skipped, 294 snapshots passed, in 596.41s. That validates the committed generated view (CHANGELOG.md) against every test that reads generated documents and version metadata.

data.how: Before filing or claiming a "config section" task: grep the planned consumers, and if they are separate items that depend on it, merge the section into the first consumer. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py -q` before committing a new knob.
data.rule: Do not slice a config section into a task of its own when its readers come later: the dead-knob ratchet (tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py) requires every documented knob to be read by code, and its allowlist may only shrink, so a section with no reader cannot pass ci. Declare the knobs in the task that first consumes them, or wire a real reader in the same change.
data.summary: B-docs-config declared eight `[docs]` knobs whose consumers (B-docs-check-command, B-docscheck-extractors) DEPEND on it, so the ci gate refused it: test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs fails for any documented knob no code reads, and its allowlist may only shrink. The fix was to abandon the item and fold the section into the consumer. Before slicing config work, check who READS each knob and whether that reader lands in the same change.
data.title: A config section must land with the code that reads it, or the dead-knob ratchet refuses it
data.why: A knob an operator can set that nothing consumes is a lie in the documentation, and the repo makes that mechanically detectable -- so the ratchet is working as designed and the SLICE was wrong, not the test.

data.alternatives: Allowlisting the eight in tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py with reasons: rejected -- that ratchet exists so a knob with no reader cannot ship, and its own file says the allowlist may only shrink. Wiring the readers now: rejected as a larger change than the slice (it is B-docs-check-command's core).
data.consequences: The section lands WITH its first reader, so no knob is ever documented without a reader. B-docs-config is abandoned (not delivered as its own item) and B-docs-check-command's globs and body grow to include the section, its test and the generated surfaces (config --explain golden, README knob table, the setup/ops transcript, and the upgrade-manifest fragments). Its branch keeps the finished work for that task to copy.
data.context: B-docs-config declared the [docs] config section (8 knobs) but nothing reads them yet: the consumers are B-docs-check-command and B-docscheck-extractors, which DEPEND on this item. The dead-knob ratchet (tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py: every documented knob must be read by code; its allowlist may only shrink) refused it, and the ci gate listed it with the manifest, remedy-text and transcript failures that any change adding these knobs must also satisfy.
data.decision: A config section is declared in the task that FIRST READS its knobs, never in a predecessor: the [docs] section moves into B-docs-check-command, which declares the section and consumes it in the same change. B-docs-config is abandoned as mis-sliced. The finished section exists on branch ddflow/B-docs-config (commits 8209c908 and 09ebbddd, tested: 15 tests plus the whole config family) for that task to copy rather than rewrite.

The same deterministic report from CLI and MCP (parity test): findings, what was checked, a digest of the report for the tree. Exit 0 clean / 1 findings / 2 could not run (never 0) / 3 refused. Hot files cli.py and mcp.py: claim only when ready to edit.

Phase B-docs-stage; decision D-docs-stage; research R-docs-stage.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: MCP: ONE `ddflow_docs` tool with a verb argument (the record-surface convention; the tools/list budget has about 2 KB of headroom), not a tool per verb. This task supplies the `check` implementation; B-dt-surfaces' check verb and B-ds-surfaces' search/read verbs delegate to it and add verbs to the same tool.

FOLDED IN (operator 2026-10-14, decision D-docs-section-with-its-reader): the `[docs]` CONFIG SECTION, which cannot land before its reader -- the dead-knob ratchet (tests/test_ratchet_no_dead_knobs.py) requires every documented knob to be read by code, and B-docs-config was abandoned for that reason. Its finished work is on branch ddflow/B-docs-config (commits 8209c908 and 09ebbddd) -- COPY it, do not rewrite it:
  * ddflow/config_sections/docs.py: DocsConfig with severity (reuses [enforce]'s BLOCK_WARN_OFF triple; default warn; strictest warn, so a typo cannot start refusing merges), check_links (off|local|network; default local; strictest local; deliberately NOT an outward value -- a link check is a read-only GET, following upgrade.release_check's own precedent), check_paths (empty = the [enforce].doc_globs minus doc_exclude set, reused rather than copied), lint_command (empty = the lint is `unavailable`, never passed), cli_command (read by B-docscheck-extractors), ignore_paths, ignore_names, and extract ([[docs.extract]] kind/pattern/source_globs, validated by extract_problem(); a malformed table is FATAL and names the entry, because an extractor that cannot fire reads exactly like a clean run).
  * tests/test_docs_config.py (15 tests), the ddflow.config re-export, the Config field and the config_sections/__init__.py SECTION_NAMES entry come with it.
READ THEM HERE: check_docs already takes doc_globs/doc_exclude/ignore_paths/ignore_names/commands, so pass the section's scope and ignore lists through; THIS task must read severity (the report's outcome), check_links (the link pass's mode) and lint_command (run it, or record it unavailable); B-docscheck-extractors reads cli_command and extract.
CHORES any change adding these knobs must also do (the ci gate on 09ebbddd found every one): regenerate tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr (the config --explain golden); regenerate the README knob table with `python -m ddflow.views.knob_table README.md` AND update its three count claims (220 knobs across 30 sections -> 228 across 31); repin tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json; and ship one knob_added.docs.<knob>.toml fragment per knob under ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ (kind/key/new/why/impact) or the release manifest lint blocks 0.2.3. Watch tests/test_remedy_texts.py: printed advice may not name a command that does not exist, so no knob doc may say `ddflow docs check` until THIS task creates it.

data.summary: `core.graph.find_cycles(items, edges)` CONSUMES the list its `edges` callable returns (it pops as the iterative DFS walks), so a caller whose `edges` returns the item's OWN list has that list silently emptied -- the item's dependencies disappear. Repro: `p = {"b": {"needs": ["a"]}}; find_cycles(p, lambda it: it["needs"])` then `p["b"]["needs"] == []` (was `["a"]`). Hit while building `core.schedule.waves` for B-gap-plan-lint: `waves` passed its own `edges` straight to `find_cycles`, so after that call every item's needs read empty and EVERY wave came out 1 -- a wrong answer, not an error. Every existing caller must already be passing a copying `edges` (the docstring insists a caller "must pass the one it will walk", which is the clue: walking costs it). Fix direction: pop from a local copy inside find_cycles (or make it not consume), so the trap cannot fire on a caller that returns the item's own list.
data.title: find_cycles consumes the edges list it is given, emptying the caller's data

data.body:
Fixes bug B693a09edfe: `core.graph.find_cycles(items, edges)` CONSUMES the list its `edges` callable returns (it pops as the iterative DFS walks), so a caller whose `edges` returns the item's OWN list has that list silently emptied -- the item's dependencies disappear. Repro: `p = {"b": {"needs": ["a"]}}; find_cycles(p, lambda it: it["needs"])` then `p["b"]["needs"] == []` (was `["a"]`). Hit while building `core.schedule.waves` for B-gap-plan-lint: `waves` passed its own `edges` straight to `find_cycles`, so after that call every item's needs read empty and EVERY wave came out 1 -- a wrong answer, not an error. Every existing caller must already be passing a copying `edges` (the docstring insists a caller "must pass the one it will walk", which is the clue: walking costs it). Fix direction: pop from a local copy inside find_cycles (or make it not consume), so the trap cannot fire on a caller that returns the item's own list. Found on B-gap-plan-lint.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B693a09edfe --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B693a09edfe --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B693a09edfe: find_cycles consumes the edges list it is given, emptying the caller's data

data.body:
WHAT: mechanical plan checking, not LLM decomposition. `ddflow plan check <file|->` takes a proposed set of phases/tasks (TOML or JSON: id, title, needs, globs, body, acceptance) and reports, before anything is filed: (1) a `*` in a directory position or a glob that matches more than N files (L-glob-overlap-is-conservative); (2) cycles and dependencies on unknown ids; (3) tasks that can run together (no dependency path between them) whose globs overlap, with the exact pair and the glob that collides, and the waves the plan would give (B-dag-waves-fanout's schedule.waves when present); (4) tasks missing acceptance, test plan or size; a task whose globs span more than K top-level directories (candidate for split); (5) duplicates against the existing queue through the add-time similar check. `ddflow plan apply` files a checked plan with one command and one transaction. The same check runs as a warning at `task add` and `phase add` so hand-filed tasks get it too. Optional flag `plan review` records a plan-review round with the existing cross-family reviewers (kind 'plan'), prompt template overridable, findings go through review triage like any review. Glob suggestion: given a title/body, list literal globs from past completed tasks whose merged files co-changed with the same words (read-only advice from worktree.merged records).

Traceability 2026-10-10 (reorg audit): this task OWNS the wave computation (B-dag-waves-fanout was narrowed to reuse it): `core.schedule.waves(items)` as a pure function over any item set (the proposed plan here; B-dag-waves-fanout later feeds it the open queue for next/board). B-dag-waves-fanout keeps only the next/board display and the mermaid DAG.

Reorganisation audit 2026-10-10: open design points: ddflow/templates/prompts/review/ does not exist (review prompts are review_system.md and review_user.md): say where a plan-review round is recorded before an item exists, or defer that flag; the add-time warning also edits ddflow/api/items.py and the README/driver text. Call the existing core/graph.find_cycles and core/globs.overlap (and the add-time similar check); share the overlap report with B-par-auto-split.

Pipeline-requirements extension 2026-10-11 (R-pipeline-configurable-today, R-pipeline-requirements-design): `plan check` also prints, per proposed task, the EFFECTIVE pipeline it would run by calling the pure resolver of B-pipe-resolve (no second implementation, no I/O); `ddflow workflow preview` (B-pipe-preview) is the same function for one hypothetical item.

PROGRESS 2026-10-14: **waves() LANDED** on branch ddflow/B-gap-plan-lint (commit 11764063): `core.schedule.waves(items, *, edges, globs_of, cap)` -- pure, wave 1 for the unblocked, one more than the deepest dependency otherwise, one wave later when a same-wave item's globs overlap (`globs.overlap`, the predicate claim refuses leases on), `cap` items per wave at most, and NO wave for items on a cycle (they can never start). tests/test_waves.py, 8 tests: the hand-computed DAG levels, a dependency LATER in the mapping, a glob conflict re-ordering two otherwise-independent items, the cap, a cycle (and what waits on it), a dependency outside the plan, order independence, and cap<1 refused. The lease was released with the branch holding this; the worktree is clean.

REMAINING (the bulk): `ddflow plan check/apply` -- ddflow/services/plancheck.py + ddflow/api/plan.py + ddflow/surfaces/declared/plan.py (declare the Command once and the CLI parser and MCP tool are generated), the add-time warning in ddflow/api/items.py, the acceptance/test-plan/size checks, the duplicate check via services/similar, and the plan-review round (the reorg audit's open point: the prompt template does not exist -- decide where a plan review is recorded before an item exists, or defer that flag). WIDEN THE GLOBS FIRST: they name paths that do not exist yet (services/plancheck.py, api/plan.py, surfaces/declared/plan.py, templates/prompts/review/plan.md, tests/test_plan_check.py), and the acceptance also names README + the driver doc, which are outside the declared globs today.

FOUND while doing it: B693a09edfe -- core.graph.find_cycles CONSUMES the list its `edges` callable returns (it pops as the DFS walks), so passing `lambda it: it["needs"]` empties the item's own dependencies and every wave came out 1. waves hands it a copy. Fix task fix-B693a09edfe.

Probe: `ddflow plan check` on a wide-glob plan (prints wide_glob, exit 1) and on a clean plan (prints the waves, exit 0); the CLI tests pin both. The acceptance's wildcard case is pinned by test_the_command_reports_a_finding_and_fails.

The repo's own rules were followed rather than excepted: the deferred_imports ratchet (my core imports moved to module level after ci named it), the leaf-vs-group exemption rule in registry.exempt_paths (written so a group word is not offered as a leaf exemption), the generated-surface pins (both CLI-help goldens regenerated, both transcripts repinned), and the README command reference (which the acceptance asks for). Lease widened twice as the work reached outside the declared globs.

Cross-family reviewer Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (alibaba; author deepseek) over the whole diff. Four findings, all REFUTED: (1) that find_cycles' list mutation leaves `needs` empty -- waves hands it a COPY (`lambda it: list(edges(it))`, with the reason in a comment) and the 8 wave tests pass; (2) that a dependency not yet placed defaults to wave 1 -- the two-pass loop places in-plan dependencies first, and a dependency OUTSIDE the plan counting as satisfied is documented and pinned by a test; (3) that plancheck.overlaps and waves disagree about a dependent overlapping pair -- by design: a pair with a dependency path is LEGAL for the check (the order is real) and waves still puts them in successive waves (deps first), so the coarser rule never mis-orders, it only spends an extra wave; (4) its own note that O.failed/O.refused map to 1/3 agrees with the code. Diff-vs-intent judged by Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 (alibaba): the intent was the mechanical plan checking of B-gap-plan-lint -- the checks, the waves this task owns, and a command to run them -- and it found no place where the diff and that intent disagree (its four findings are the refuted set above). Filed when B-gap-plan-lint completed (merged ee236d36): its WHAT listed these and its ACCEPTANCE did not, so they were NOT implemented and must not be lost with the done item. 1. `ddflow plan apply `: file a checked plan with one command and ONE transaction (atomic: killed mid-way, nothing half-filed). Refuse when `plan check` has findings. 2. The add-time WARNING at `ddflow task add` / `phase add`: the same checks as a warning on hand-filed items (plancheck.check already takes `tracked`/`similar`; a warning must NOT change an exit code). 3. The duplicate hunt: inject `services.similar` as plancheck.check's `similar` parameter (the parameter exists and is tested; `api/plan.py` passes nothing for it today). 4. The optional `plan review` round: the reorg audit's open point -- the prompt path the body named (ddflow/templates/prompts/review/plan.md) does not exist; decide where a plan review is recorded BEFORE an item exists, or defer the flag explicitly. 5. THE P-GAPS ACCEPTANCE CHECK, never run: build a plan from the 11 P-gaps tasks (`ddflow --json show ` per task: needs/globs/body) and require PC.check to report zero findings. `ddflow --json list task --phase

` did not return a `.rows` key when tried; use --limit 1000 or per-id `show`. 6. The driver-doc sentence (the README half landed): docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md should say to run plan check before filing a phase. GLOBS: ddflow/api/plan.py, ddflow/services/plancheck.py, ddflow/api/items.py, ddflow/surfaces/declared/plan.py, tests/test_plan_apply.py, tests/test_plan_check.py, docs/ddflow/drivers/implement-phase.md.

data.summary: config_sections/_kinds.py says '[gates].kind_pipelines replaces [the pipeline] per kind, so a document, a research item or a scheduled job gets its own gates', but 'ddflow task add --help' offers no --kind (options: --title --needs --globs --tags --body --priority --line --phase --parent --lines --port-of ...). In run_nemo_run a task whose whole content was the generated output of 'ddflow upgrade --apply' (DDFLOWUP021.1) and a one-section docs/RESEARCH.md entry (DECMODEL.0) had to run the code-task pipeline: 'ddflow complete' refuses with 'required gate(s) not passed: implement, unit_tests' and 'reviewer independence not satisfied: no reviewer ran at all' after every gate was skipped on the record, so the only exits are --force or leaving the item running with a lease. Fix: 'task add --kind doc' (and research/job) wired to kind_pipelines, with a shipped default doc pipeline that does not require unit_tests.

data.summary: Reproduced in run_nemo_run 0.2.1 on 2026-10-16: 'ddflow merge DECMODEL.11' was still running minutes after its merge commit landed, and a concurrent 'ddflow complete DECMODEL.11' (and any other write) failed after 30 s with 'TimeoutError: could not acquire /ai/delian/src/run_nemo_run/.ddflow/events.lock within 30s ... Held by pid 783395 (python3 -m ddflow merge DECMODEL.11). Another agent may be wedged, or the machine is overloaded'. The earlier merges (DDFLOWUP021.1, DECMODEL.0) ran past a 120 s tool timeout the same way. The lock should cover appending events, not a multi-minute subprocess (the likely cause is the new [ci].on_merge health check, default 'fast'). With several agents on one repository this serialises the whole fleet behind one merge and makes the 'wedged agent' message misleading. Fix: release the lock around the post-merge check, record its outcome as a later event, and print when the check starts. Related to merge-silent-during-post-merge-ci (same cause, different symptom).
data.title: ddflow merge holds .ddflow/events.lock for the whole post-merge run, so every other ddflow command in the project times out

data.summary: DEFAULT_COMMAND in ddflow/services/ci*.py is 'pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files', and [ci].on_merge='fast' runs the same set after each merge. A hook with 'language: fail' and a 'files:' pattern is a commit-time tripwire (fires when a STAGED path matches); run over all files it fails whenever the frozen paths exist at all. In run_nemo_run the hook frozen-workflow-files made 'ci on master: FAILED: workflow files frozen since the ddflow cutover' on every merge (DDFLOWUP021.1, DECMODEL.0, DECMODEL.11) and filed the bug Bci-workflow-files-frozen-since-th-8c9a18373d. Probed: 'pre-commit run frozen-workflow-files --all-files' lists the frozen docs and fails; '--from-ref HEAD~1 --to-ref HEAD' skips it ('no files to check'). The repo-side fix is 'stages: [pre-commit]' on the hook, but ddflow should not make a tripwire the project wrote red by default. Fix: run merge-time CI over the merge's changed range (--from-ref <base> --to-ref HEAD) instead of --all-files, or skip 'language: fail' hooks, and say in the failure message which hook and which files.
data.title: default CI command runs commit-time tripwire hooks over every tracked file, so merge-time CI is red by construction

data.claim: Keep the in-house tomllib+tomlkit loader and add dynaconf's capabilities to it: a packaged default.toml, sorted .ddflow/conf.d/*.toml drop-ins with replace/extend semantics and per-key origin, a managed drop-in for tool-written changes (comments preserved), lazy code-free ${...} interpolation, Jinja (sandboxed, extension allowlist, imported only when a template marker is present) and a compiled config cache. Dynaconf itself is a poor fit: +70-150 ms import and 12-15 MB per command (the hook path), loaders.write drops TOML comments, @jinja/@format/hooks can read the environment or execute code, no Jinja extension hook, and D-unify caps runtime dependencies at two.
data.falsifier: Wrong if the compiled cache plus lazy sections cannot keep Config.load under the hook latency budget, or if a drop-in directory makes provenance and merge conflicts worse than one file.
data.mechanism: Config today: 35 sections, 314 knobs with Python dataclass defaults; layers default < committed .ddflow/config.toml < local < env; flow.* choices recorded in the log fill only unset knobs; no user/system layer; gates/reviewers/companions already load from per-topic files via a hand-written filename list; config.toml re-read 3-4 times per command, no cache; import ddflow.config 80-100 ms, Config.load about 2 ms, ddflow --version 0.72 s. B-org-layers (one layer stack) and B-org-bundle (a bundle mirrors .ddflow/) already describe the requested default.toml + conf.d layout, so it is their foundation, not a second mechanism.
data.probe: Two read-only research passes 2026-10-17 (web, installed dynaconf 3.3.5 in a scratch dir, measured import time and memory, source reading of @jinja/@format/hooks; internal code reading and timing). Not verified: dynaconf thread safety, systemd-analyze cat-config/cargo --show-origin details, direnv/mise hash details, pydantic-settings deep merge, dynaconf behaviour on Python 3.11, measurements are single-machine best-of-three. Operator decisions 2026-10-17 are in D-config-engine (full Jinja everywhere is the operator's choice against the research advice; knob [config].template_trust lets a user or org tighten it).
data.question: How should ddflow's configuration become layered (packaged default.toml, project config.toml, .ddflow/conf.d drop-ins), dynamic (templates, interpolation), persistent for tool-written changes, and fast, and is dynaconf the right engine?

data.body: Replace Config.load's hard-coded order by a declared stack: packaged default.toml < system/org < user < project .ddflow/conf.d/*.toml (sorted) < project config.toml < machine-local conf.d and config < env < CLI. This is the mechanism B-org-layers describes: implement it ONCE here and make B-org-layers consume it (fold B-org-layers' stack work into this task if the scopes coincide, keep its org-source parts). data.body: Operator decision D-config-engine: full Jinja is allowed in ANY config file, with extensions. Implement: values marked as templates (`{{ ... }}` / `{% ... %}` or an explicit `@jinja` prefix) are rendered lazily at read in a SandboxedEnvironment by default; extensions are loaded by dotted module name from `[config].jinja_extensions` (an allowlist), globals/filters registered by name from config and by installed packages; jinja2 is imported only when a template marker is present (hook path cost); `[config].template_trust = any|digest|off` (default any, the operator's choice) lets a user/org tighten it to approved digests (direnv-allow style, stored in .ddflow/local) or off; `ddflow doctor` notes a committed config using templates and which trust mode applies. Tests: untrusted-template hazards under each mode, sandbox escapes (os, subprocess, attribute walks) refused in sandbox mode, lazy import verified. data.body: Today the committed config.toml is re-read 3-4 times per command and nothing is cached. Contradictions found by the 2026-10-17 roadmap review (six reviewers over the whole open queue; 56 entries). Each needs either a decision amendment (operator), a task rewrite, or a note that it is intended. Resolve in order of confidence; decision amendments need the operator (use the ask engine). Never settle a decision task by abandoning it while a task still lists it in needs.

[high] D-failed-critic-not-blocking, D-failed-review-gate, D-review-triage, D-review-budget, D-merge-order-warn: D-failed-critic-not-blocking (accepted, early Oct) says complete accepts a failed critic and 'do not add a complete-time refusal'; D-review-triage says 'no new completion block'; D-review-budget (4) says a not-converged review only prints a NOTE and never blocks; D-merge-order-warn says merge only warns. D-failed-review-gate (2026-10-17, operator, bug B85841c0846) is the opposite: merge AND complete REFUSE a required review gate whose latest outcome is failed unless every confirmed finding has a later delta round that did not re-raise it, or the operator overrides with a recorded reason. Both  => PROPOSED: D-failed-review-gate governs (later, explicit operator, newer evidence). Supersede D-failed-critic-not-blocking with a record that keeps its still-true part ('failed' is an outcome that satisfies every-gate-has-an-outcome; the cross-family rule still applies) and states: 'complete and merge refuse a failed review gate with an unre-reviewed confirmed finding (D-failed-review-gate); a gate settled by triage with all findings refuted passes'. Amend D-review-triage (drop 'no new completion block'), 

[high] B-review-convergence, D-failed-review-gate, D-failed-critic-not-blocking, fix-B85841c0846: Open task B-review-convergence requires that 'complete and merge print a NOTE when not converged and NEVER block (D-failed-critic-not-blocking)' with a failing-first acceptance test 'the NOTE appears and does not block'. fix-B85841c0846 and D-failed-review-gate (accepted 2026-10-17) make merge and complete refuse exactly that state. Whichever lands second breaks the other's test. => PROPOSED: Rewrite B-review-convergence acceptance: the 'converged' flag shown in gate status and brief uses the same predicate as fix-B85841c0846 (every confirmed finding followed by a later delta round that did not re-raise it); not converged = merge/complete refuse (exit 3) unless the recorded operator override; drop 'NEVER block' and the D-failed-critic-not-blocking citation.
