[medium] B-rules-onto-record-surface, P-core-records.engine: B-rules-onto-record-surface (old, p12 but held behind the docs wave) ends with 'either declare lessons, bugs, items and research as RecordKinds, or record a decision that they stay hand-written'; P-core-records.engine (p16, earlier) is exactly 'put bug, lesson, research, memory, task, phase on the RecordKind descriptor'. => PROPOSED: P-core-records.engine owns it; delete that clause from B-rules-onto-record-surface (rules and the weakening/ack/recall rows stay) and add the need (above).

[low] B-export-onboard, B-dt-onboard: B-dt-onboard's body (traceability 2026-10-10) says B-export-onboard is 'expected to be closed as covered' and that it carries the whole acceptance; B-export-onboard says it is probably obsolete and to check first, yet D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted records the edge 'B-export-onboard needs B-dt-onboard and B-tpl-adopt' (so it is meant to survive as a follow-up). => PROPOSED: Leave as is until B-export-onboard is ready (operator 2026-10-10 told the agent to check the successor first and complete with a gate skip citing it); no change now.

[low] LB-surfaces, D-labels: LB-surfaces title says `ddflow label add|rm|rename|...` while its body says `ddflow tag add|rm|...` (alias `ddflow label`); D-labels says a label IS a tag. Two names for the one command group on the MCP tools/list budget. => PROPOSED: Decide in LB-surfaces which is canonical (tag as the group, label as the alias, or the reverse) and make title and body agree; do not ship two MCP tools.

[low] B-rc-lifecycle, B-rc-lifecycle-guard: B-rc-lifecycle's body still lists items (7) weakening flag/ack and (8) read-only sources in WHAT, HOW TO TEST and ACCEPTANCE although the header says they moved to B-rc-lifecycle-guard; the guard's body lists them again. A reader of the running task can build them twice. => PROPOSED: Strike (7)/(8) and the ack/readonly tests from B-rc-lifecycle's body once it is merged, or note 'moved' inline; no queue change needed.

[high] PM-descriptor, PM-kilo, PM-docs, PM-acceptance, D-platform-mcp: D-platform-mcp (accepted 2026-10-13) says the Kilo entry and similar platform entries are ENABLED BY DEFAULT once the agent is onboarded (a knob turns it off). The titles/bodies of PM-descriptor ('adopt writes it disabled ... enabled false'), PM-kilo (title 'adopt writes the remote mcp.kilo entry disabled'; 'Only after an operator enables it'), and PM-acceptance ('Kilo entry written disabled, enabled by the operator') still say disabled; PM-docs promises an 'operator guide to enabling Kilo MCP safely'. Appended D-platform-mcp notes in the bodies contradict the first paragraph in the same task. => PROPOSED: Rewrite the titles and first paragraphs of PM-descriptor, PM-kilo, PM-acceptance and PM-docs to the decided behaviour (written enabled for an onboarded agent, guard mandatory, [platform].auto_enable knob, acceptance asserts the guard refuses delete/billable/cross-org calls and that auto_enable=false writes it disabled).

[high] P-agent-parity.kimi-suite, D-kimi: kimi-suite says 'at the tier the operator chooses', but D-kimi (1) decided tier 1 (live headless smoke, 3 USD cap, majority of 3, weekly, plus fixtures). The task would reopen a settled choice. => PROPOSED: Edit the body: tier 1 per D-kimi; the [test] section of kimi.toml follows B-ac-smoke's tier-1 criteria.

[medium] P-agent-parity.kimi-hooks, P-agent-parity.kimi-launcher, P-agent-parity.kimi-meters, P-agent-parity.kimi-subagents-skills, P-agent-parity.kimi-acp, P-agent-parity.kimi-server, B-hx-migrate, B-hx-hook-writers, B-hx-guide: The kimi tasks create per-agent code modules (hookwriters/kimi*.py, launch/kimi*.py, meters/kimi*.py, skillsync_kimi*.py, lanes/kimi_acp*.py, lanes/kimi_server*.py). B-hx-hook-writers is explicitly 'by style, not by agent'; B-hx-migrate adds a lint test that fails on a hard-coded agent name or harness path outside ddflow/harnesses/; P-agent-parity.new-descriptors/B-hx-guide say agents are data ('no agent code'). The kimi-launcher is also redundant with kimi-descriptor's [headless] section (the launcher already instantiates descriptor templates). => PROPOSED: Reword globs and scope: a 'toml-hooks' hook-writer style (hookwriters/toml_hooks.py), a generic 'stream-json' event mapper (launch/streamjson.py, shared with claude -p and codex exec), meters as a descriptor [meters] entry read by the registry, skill/agent sync through the generic B-skills-sync/B-sub-sync with a kimi path entry, and the ACP/server backends as descriptor [acp] data plus the generic backend. Reduce kimi-launcher to the stream-json mapper and a launcher-template entry; kimi-meters 

[medium] P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2, P-agent-lifecycle.detect, B-am-harness-probe, P-governor.facts, P-agent-parity.meters, P-context-sync.doors, P-spawn.descriptor, B-ac-smoke, AC-registry, PM-descriptor, OB-verify-facts, AC-spike, PL-probe, CP-verify-facts, P-spawn.facts: Fifteen tasks define or probe overlapping descriptor sections with no owner: [detect] (descriptor-v2 and P-agent-lifecycle.detect), [telemetry] vs [transcripts] (descriptor-v2 vs B-am-harness-probe), [meters] vs [governor] context_meter/quota_meter (descriptor-v2/P-agent-parity.meters vs P-governor.facts), the hook-event/door set probed four times (B-am-harness-probe canonical events, P-context-sync.doors [doors], P-governor.facts safe_point_hooks, B-hx-research matrix), [headless] vs B-ac-smoke [test], plus [spawn], [acp], [platform]. Six probe tasks (OB-verify-facts, AC-spike, PL-probe, CP-v => PROPOSED: Make P-agent-parity.descriptor-v2 (priority 22) the single schema owner: reserve every section name now (detect, headless, continuation, meters, caps, autonomy, telemetry/transcripts, spawn, doors, acp, platform, governor, test) with one definition of each fact; later tasks only fill values and may not add or rename a section. One generated facts table (CP-verify-facts style) fed by all the probes; the others add_need on descriptor-v2 (edges proposed above).

[medium] B-ac-smoke, P-agent-parity.launcher, P-agent-parity.suite, B-ac-fixtures: B-ac-smoke (priority 32) builds its own headless runner (scripts/ci/agent-smoke, services/agent_smoke.py, [test] templates) while P-agent-parity.launcher (45) describes itself as 'one engine for dispatch, restarts, smoke tests, remote control' and P-agent-parity.suite runs the scenario 'through the launcher'. Two runners will exist for the same headless invocation, session-id capture and event-stream parsing. => PROPOSED: B-ac-smoke builds the minimal runner on descriptor [headless]; launcher then adopts it (launcher needs B-ac-smoke, or B-ac-smoke's runner module is the launcher's start verb). State this in both bodies; P-agent-parity.suite already needs both.

[medium] P-agent-parity.tool-profile, PM-search-call, CP-mcp-profiles, SE-mcp-budget, P-agent-caps.slots, P-spawn.engine, P-context-sync.tell: (1) P-agent-parity.tool-profile says 'make the remaining tools reachable by a single dispatcher tool for capped clients' while PM-search-call builds exactly that facade (ddflow_search/ddflow_call) at priority 59; two dispatchers with the same file (surfaces/mcp.py). (2) Every P-sdd/P-plan-modes task says 'add no MCP tool, ~45 bytes of headroom' and SE-mcp-budget says the list is nearly full, yet P-agent-caps.slots (new tool ddflow_slot), P-spawn.engine and P-context-sync.tell ('one MCP tool') and PM-search-call (two tools) each add tools without needing SE-mcp-budget or saying they join an exi => PROPOSED: tool-profile keeps the cap-driven tier choice and defers the dispatcher to PM-search-call (say so in tool-profile; PM-search-call already reaches tool-profile through CP-mcp-profiles). The three tool-adding tasks become actions inside existing groups (SE-mcp-budget rule) and add_need SE-mcp-budget (report-only, priority 22) so the byte cost is reported when they land.

[medium] OB-rules-glob, B-path-rules-to-decisions, B-rules-import, SDD-rules-bridge, OB-agents-others: B-rules-import (boundary note 2026-10-10) says a path-scoped rule file (frontmatter globs) is owned by B-path-rules-to-decisions and becomes a DECISION referencing the file; B-rules-import skips it so a file is never imported twice. OB-rules-glob ('Claude paths, Cursor .mdc types, Copilot applyTo, Windsurf/Devin glob, Cline paths, Continue, Kiro fileMatch') imports/emits glob rules as rule records, and SDD-rules-bridge imports Kiro steering (fileMatch) and Spec Kit constitution as 'rule candidates, never decisions'; OB-agents-others also lists 'Kiro steering modes' as native. The same path-sco => PROPOSED: Single boundary: always-on files -> rules (B-rules-import); path-scoped files -> decision-with-globs by reference (B-path-rules-to-decisions) for the IMPORT side in every dialect (OB-rules-glob adds the dialect parsers to the rule_globs family and owns the EMIT side with the manifest). SDD-rules-bridge narrows to the Spec Kit constitution.md (one adapter-table row plus rules export into .specify/memory/constitution.md); Kiro steering import/export is done by OB-rules-glob and OB-agents-others (k

[medium] PL-native-export, SDD-export-tasks, PL-slice, PL-mirror: Three tasks write the same Kiro tasks.md: SDD-export-tasks (kiro flavour, region mode, checkbox state from task state), PL-native-export (.kiro/specs/ddflow-<label>/{requirements,design,tasks}.md) and PL-mirror (checkbox write-back). PL-slice and SDD-export-tasks both render a slice of queue tasks as a markdown checklist. D-sdd-plan-modes says native todo lists are mirrors and execution stays in the loop. => PROPOSED: One renderer (PL-slice projection + SDD-export-tasks formats). PL-native-export only decides WHERE a flavour is written per agent; PL-mirror's Kiro checkbox write-back is the existing export in region mode with ddflow owning the state (SDD-export-tasks), behind the knob, not a second writer.

[medium] SDD-model, OB-native-only, OB-model, D-ai-import, D-sdd-plan-modes: SDD-model defines a spec-source record kind (tool, path, digest, version, trust=imported) and OB-native-only lists 'Kiro specs, Spec Kit and OpenSpec trees' as pointer-plus-digest records (OB-model also gives trust=imported, origin digest and source path on every record). D-ai-import changed OB-native-only from pointer-only to managed. Research question 9 (does P-sdd absorb OB-native-only's Kiro/Spec Kit/OpenSpec items) was never answered in D-sdd-plan-modes. Result: two record kinds for the same tree, and a task title (OB-native-only: 'never emitted') that contradicts its own D-ai-import note => PROPOSED: SDD-model owns the spec-source kind; OB-native-only's spec-tree classes are instances of it (edge proposed). Retitle OB-native-only to 'Managed non-instruction classes: permissions and sandbox, hooks, plugins, output styles, off-disk team/org rules, auto memories (widening flag at plan review)' and remove the spec-tree classes from its list; SDD-import emits the records and the plan, OB-eval keeps the fixtures.

[high] B-org-trust, D-org-config: D-org-config (2) says a project's own config may declare company sources with NO machine allowlist, signatures optional; B-org-trust says 'a project cannot introduce a source the machine does not allow ... the allowlist lives in [REDACTED:path] or /etc/ddflow/org.toml, never in the project'. => PROPOSED: Follow the decision (operator 2026-10-06): the machine allowlist is optional and only restricts when present; safety comes from digest-approved executable content and the requirement of a valid signature for auto_apply = enforced. Rewrite the B-org-trust first sentence and tests; the 'cloned repo names an attacker's org' case is covered by inert-until-approved, not by an allowlist.

[high] B-review-convergence, D-failed-review-gate: B-review-convergence says complete and merge print a NOTE when not converged 'and NEVER block (D-failed-critic-not-blocking)'. D-failed-review-gate (operator 2026-10-17) makes merge and complete REFUSE a required review gate whose latest outcome is failed until confirmed findings are re-reviewed (fix rounds free). D-failed-critic-not-blocking is the earlier stance. => PROPOSED: Rewrite B-review-convergence: 'converged' reuses the D-failed-review-gate predicate in services/gates/outcomes.py (confirmed finding followed by a delta round that did not re-raise it) and the NOTE explains the refusal; the time-budget partial stays non-blocking only for the unreviewed-chunks case. Also its 'round n/max' must use the fix_round_free rule.

[medium] DX-watch-job, P-schedule.watch, DX-health-watch: Three tasks name the CLI noun `ddflow watch`: DX-watch-job (wait for a job/file/pid while renewing leases), P-schedule.watch (upstream-change watch records, declared/watch.py), and DX-health-watch's text (`ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack`). The watchdog was in fact built as `ddflow health` (surfaces/declared/health.py). => PROPOSED: Keep `ddflow watch` for P-schedule.watch (a record kind with add/edit verbs, D-schedule-early) ; DX-watch-job becomes `ddflow wait --job/--file/--pid/--gate` (its own text says reuse ddflow wait) or `ddflow job watch`; fix the stale CLI name in DX-health-watch's body and DX-health-watch-liveness.

[high] DX-dispatch-supervise, DX-health-watch, D-lease-break-explicit: Two ladders. DX-health-watch's CORRECT ladder is nudge -> ask status -> request yield -> park -> take over/relaunch -> escalate, with act|advise modes; DX-dispatch-supervise (amended 2026-10-15 to consume the watchdog) still lists 'nudge the lane, request yield, take over, relaunch' and its own stall = no progress watermark for [dispatch].stall_s while another item waits. It also takes over with 'recover and claim --force', but D-lease-break-explicit made the sanctioned break `ddflow claim --break` (break_on_timeout default false). => PROPOSED: One owner per step: the watchdog owns detection and the nudge/yield/park/escalate ladder (and [watch].act); DX-dispatch-supervise owns only refill-after-merge, RESUME/relaunch (via DX-park-and-resume) and merge order, and uses `claim --break` for take-over only when policy allows. Delete [dispatch].stall_s in favour of [watch].stall_s.

[medium] DX-dispatch-launch, DM-kinds, D-daemons: D-daemons (1) lists five kinds ddflow may start: scheduler tick, watchers, serve, hub mirror, lane supervisor. DM-kinds ships scheduler tick, serve, hub mirror, watchers and omits the lane supervisor; DX-dispatch-launch ships ddflow/templates/daemons/lane-supervisor.toml before the daemon record kind exists. DM-kinds also ships a hub mirror kind while KB-mirror (prio 64) does not exist. => PROPOSED: DM-kinds owns the template files for kinds whose command exists: scheduler tick, watchers, serve, lane supervisor (calling DX-dispatch-launch's tick). The hub-mirror kind template moves to KB-mirror (add a need KB-mirror -> DM-kinds).

[medium] P-agent-parity.launcher, DM-lifecycle, DM-supervisors, CP-backend-iface, P-spawn.engine: 'One supervisor, not three': the launcher is a detached supervisor over `ddflow job run`; DM-lifecycle/DM-supervisors define a pidfile + backoff supervisor with its own adapter interface (start, stop, status, logs; child process, systemd, launchd, tmux, container); CP-backend-iface defines a lane backend interface (start, steer, report, stop, status; process, tmux, paseo, opencode, orca, acp) and CP-backend-tmux is needed by DM-supervisors. Two registries and two tmux adapters. => PROPOSED: Single process layer: jobs engine + launcher 'process' backend. CP-backend-iface is the one registry; a daemon is a long-lived lane of kind=daemon whose adapter set is a subset (start, stop, status, logs); DM-supervisors then only adds the systemd/launchd unit emitters (consent) and DM-lifecycle only the pidfile lock, restart cap 3 and policy (D-daemons). Add needs DM-lifecycle -> P-agent-parity.launcher and DM-supervisors -> CP-backend-iface (already transitive through CP-backend-tmux).

[medium] P-safeguards.dispatch, DX-dispatch-plan, DX-agent-brief, P-spawn.context, B-gap-lanes: Four brief renderers for one purpose: `ddflow lanes brief` (done), `ddflow brief --for-agent` (DX-agent-brief, done), `ddflow dispatch brief <item> --role` (P-safeguards.dispatch, same command noun and files as DX-dispatch-plan), and the dispatch brief of P-spawn.context (services/lanes/brief.py). => PROPOSED: services/agent_brief.py is the renderer; P-safeguards.dispatch adds the role/safeguards/envelope sections to it (and the `dispatch brief` subcommand under DX-dispatch-plan's package); P-spawn.context and the planner call it; services/lanes/brief.py stays the ledger view.

[medium] P-schedule.unattended, DX-dispatch-launch, P-schedule.executor-basic, D-dispatch-modes: Two owners for 'start headless lanes for ready items within caps when nobody is there': P-schedule.unattended (executor + lane launcher + caps + quota guard) and DX-dispatch-launch (mode launch, tick, caps, guards, operator-only). D-dispatch-modes also requires a kill switch and schedule.max_parallel_tasks as the cap; DX-dispatch-launch mentions neither. => PROPOSED: DX-dispatch-launch owns the tick that starts lanes; P-schedule.unattended only registers/emits an executor that runs it and detects the silent no-fire. Add 'kill switch ([dispatch].enabled / `ddflow dispatch off`) and schedule.max_parallel_tasks cap' to DX-dispatch-launch's acceptance.

[high] GV-kimi-reviewer, D-kimi, GV-kimi-models: D-kimi (5) records that the operator asked for the Kimi reviewer immediately and that GV-kimi-reviewer 'is moved up'; the task sits at prio 50 behind GV-kimi-models -> P-governor.model-registry -> B-ac-smoke/B-sub-model and GV-capabilities. A kimi-k3 reviewer entry (family moonshot, gates empty) is already in the local reviewers.toml and the family is in config_sections/agent.py, so part of the task is probably done operationally; DX-reviewer-failover came out of the Kimi 5-hour quota running out. => PROPOSED: Drop the GV-kimi-models edge, prio 33; reduce the task to: moonshot in reviewers detect, sensitivity gate before sending the diff, unavailable-not-passed on a missing key/endpoint, and the failover list (DX-reviewer-failover). Verify what the existing entry already covers before building.

[medium] B-lease-edit-only-hold, D-lease-break-explicit, D-lease-hold-limit: B-lease-edit-only-hold (prio 100) still specifies break_on_timeout default true and says the claim logic is unbuilt; D-lease-break-explicit set the default false (explicit `claim --break`) and DX-lease-progress-breakable (done) built hold_max_s/break_on_timeout in config_sections/lease.py and the break. Its part (c) merge reconciliation is unbuilt (grep: no merge.reconciled/reconcile_tests). => PROPOSED: Narrow it to lease.overlap events, `ddflow lease break|keep` surfaces and the briefs; fold (c) into B-lease-reconcile-merge; update the break_on_timeout default; order after B-lease-hold-visibility as today.

[low] FL-roster, FL-surfaces: FL-roster declares `ddflow agents list|show|set` on every surface itself; FL-surfaces ('ddflow fleet|fanout|agents|receipt') is the task that declares those commands (ddflow/surfaces/declared/fleet*.py). Two owners of the `agents` verb. => PROPOSED: FL-roster ships the record kind and service (RC1-RC12) only; FL-surfaces declares `agents`. Also check the `agents` noun against P-subagents' `ddflow agent` commands before declaring.

[medium] B-upstream-detectors, B-trigger-events: Both add an uncaught-exception capture: B-upstream-detectors puts catch-alls in cli.main / MCP serve that classify an internal exception and store a last-failure record; B-trigger-events adds 'crash/exception report (ddflow report crash + hook for uncaught tracebacks, ties B-upstream-detectors)'. => PROPOSED: B-upstream-detectors owns the classifier and the last-failure record and emits one crash event kind; B-trigger-events only registers that event as a trigger source (no second hook, no `ddflow report crash`).

[medium] DX-phase-review, D-phase-review, GV-roles, P-governor.tier-suggest: D-phase-review uses `tier:fast` as a RISK/depth label for per-item review (one combined round); the same tag is the governor's model-tier hint (tier:fast|balanced|deep, advisory, set by P-governor.tier-suggest and moved by the governor ladder). Also GV-roles says planner 'strong', while D-governor fixed the names fast|balanced|deep. A model-tier downshift at 40-60 % quota would silently turn on single-round review. => PROPOSED: Use a separate review-depth label/knob (e.g. risk:low or [review].depth by glob) not derived from the model tier, or state in DX-phase-review that review depth reads only a human-set tier tag, never the governor's effective tier (GV-guardrails: floors never relaxed). Use the registry tier names fast|balanced|deep in GV-roles.

[medium] B-sched-due, B-sched-run, P-schedule.executor-basic, P-schedule.unattended, P-schedule.chain, P-schedule.outcomes, D-schedule-early: D-schedule-early governs ddflow/services/schedule/** (a package) and P-schedule.executor-basic/unattended/chain/outcomes create ddflow/services/schedule/executor.py, chain.py, history.py, while B-sched-due/-run/-defaults/-escalation edit the module ddflow/services/schedule.py. A package directory shadows the module of the same name; B-sched-emitters already chose a flat name (services/schedule_emit.py). P-schedule.executor-basic and P-schedule.unattended also both claim executor.py and surfaces/declared/schedule.py. => PROPOSED: Either make the first schedule task (B-sched-due, prio 15) convert schedule.py into the package with a facade and have the later ones use it, or use flat names (schedule_executor.py, schedule_chain.py, schedule_history.py). P-schedule.unattended should extend executor-basic's module, not redefine it.

[low] B-sched-compaction, P-lessons.curate, B-coh-sweep: B-sched-compaction (weekly job: find lessons, instructions, tasks, bugs that are duplicated/contradictory/closable) and P-lessons.curate (a lessons pass that verifies, deduplicates, retires stale ones, proposes merges) overlap on lessons; both sit on the retroactive coherence sweep (B-coh-sweep). => PROPOSED: P-lessons.curate is the lessons-specific candidate generator and report; B-sched-compaction is the scheduling wrapper over B-coh-sweep and P-lessons.curate output for lessons (add a need B-sched-compaction -> P-lessons.curate when planned).

[medium] DX-dispatch-launch, D-dispatch-modes: D-dispatch-modes requires a kill switch and schedule.max_parallel_tasks as the cap; DX-dispatch-launch/-plan do not mention a kill switch; D-dispatch-modes governs ddflow/services/dispatch/** but the tasks' globs are flat modules. => PROPOSED: Add a kill-switch knob and command to DX-dispatch-launch and the package globs (see narrow_globs).

[medium] TF-record, TD-import-core: JUnit XML ingest is in both: TF-record ('JUnit XML ingest, summary plus hash, repeats, seed, SUT pin') and TD-import-core ('Importers: JUnit XML, Cucumber, Robot ... registry adapters'). TD-import-core needs TF-record, so it must not re-implement JUnit. => PROPOSED: TF-record owns the record shape and the JUnit reader as the first row; TD-import-core registers it in the importer registry and adds Cucumber, Robot and per-scenario importers only; say so in both bodies.

[medium] SC-style-codeguide, P-safeguards.style-cards: SC-style-codeguide's title says 'style cards derived from the project's own tool configs found by the probe'; that is the deliverable of P-safeguards.style-cards ([tool.ruff] etc. to a committed card per language). SC-style-codeguide's body says it only feeds the cards and the consult action. => PROPOSED: Limit SC-style-codeguide to proposing which codeguide languages and context7 libraries to enable from the stack profile and registering them for the consult action; the cards stay with P-safeguards.style-cards. Retitle.

[medium] AI-lifecycle, CN-roles, CN-cr: AI-lifecycle plans 'a deprecated module version notifies its consumers with a deadline'; CN-roles records 'a deprecation window unless waived' and CN-cr is the consumer-notification record with per-consumer burndown. Two notification paths for the same event. => PROPOSED: A deprecation notice is a change request of kind deprecation (deadline = the window), delivered by CN-cr/CN-states; AI-lifecycle adds only the app-infra triggers (decommission, secret rotation by reference) and the destroy-plan approval.

[medium] B-lease-edit-only-hold, DX-lease-progress-breakable: B-lease-edit-only-hold (D-lease-hold-limit) is still open with the full design: [lease].hold_max_s, break_on_timeout, reconcile_tests, lease.overlap, `lease break/keep`. DX-lease-progress-breakable (DONE) already shipped hold_max_s, idle_max_s and break_on_timeout in config_sections/lease.py and a claim --break that records lease.expired and keeps the holder's branch (verified in the code). B-lease-edit-only-hold's model differs: the waiter's claim goes through with BOTH leases live (lease.overlap) and a full reconcile test run at merge, versus the shipped one-holder-breaks model. => PROPOSED: Rewrite B-lease-edit-only-hold to the part not built (reconcile_tests after a merge over another item's files, `lease keep --for N`, operator `lease break`) or abandon it in favour of DX-park-and-resume (restore) plus DX-lease-yield-doctor-status; decide which model stands by an operator decision. Its needs include the done P-unify and B-lease-hold-visibility.

[medium] DX-dispatch-launch, P-agent-parity.launcher, P-agent-parity.continuation, CP-backend-iface: DX-dispatch-launch (priority 55, tagged feature/dispatch) needs three feature tasks (P-agent-parity.launcher, P-agent-parity.continuation, CP-backend-iface). The rule 'DX-*/fix-* tasks never need a feature' is violated, and a DX id at 55 is mis-banded. The other DX-dispatch-* tasks (plan, nudge, supervise, acceptance) correctly stay in the DX band and do not depend on it. => PROPOSED: Keep the edges (they are real prerequisites) but re-file the task outside the DX namespace (e.g. P-agent-parity.dispatch-launch, same body and needs) and abandon DX-dispatch-launch as a rename; do not make DX-dispatch-acceptance need it (it does not today).

[medium] RH-place-unphased, DX-default-priority-for-dx, D-old-work-behind-core-docs-accepted: RH-place-unphased says to move fix-test-duration-* and fix-ci-split-slow-tests into a new P-test-speed phase, but its own 2026-10-16 STALE NOTE says fix/DX tasks keep their own track and need no phase, and D-old-work-behind-core-docs says any fix- item carries no hold (a new phase would inherit phase needs and hold them). P-test-robustness (12 tasks) already exists for test economy. Its list also names done tasks (B-log-snapshot-knobs). => PROPOSED: Do NOT create P-test-speed or move fix-* tasks. Reduce RH-place-unphased to the non-fix, non-DX unphased open tasks (recount below).
data.title: Resolve the 56 contradictions between decisions and tasks found by the 2026-10-17 roadmap review

data.body:
Notes from the 2026-10-17 roadmap review that were not turned into edges (87 entries): overlaps to watch, low-confidence ideas, things the reviewers could not verify. Triage each: apply it, file it as its own task, or drop it with a reason.

data.context: Operator request 2026-10-17; builds on B-upstream-reporting, P-goals (B-prop-*), P-autopilot, the cadence passes.
data.decision: PROPOSED 2026-10-17 from the operator's request (verbatim in the session log). (1) PERIODIC ROADMAP REVIEW becomes a standard periodic pass of the default pipeline (`roadmap_review`: by completed tasks, by days and at phase end), shipped in the defaults for every project: it prepares the data, runs domain reviewers as read-only lanes, validates their proposals mechanically (unknown ids, cycles, fix/DX edges to features, closed targets), then APPLIES only according to the pass mode: `propose` (default: proposals are filed for the operator) or `apply` (edges, priorities and glob narrowings above a confidence floor; merges, abandons and decision changes always need the operator), always with a before-state snapshot and a rollback. (2) SELF-IMPROVEMENT LOOP: every agent self-monitors ddflow (rule r-ddflow-self-assessment, DX-auto-assessment) and turns bugs, missing features, misbehaviour and repeated manual work into proposals through ONE path (`ddflow improve`): checked for duplicates against the local queue and upstream first; with access to the ddflow source it files into the ddflow repository's own queue (never pushes, never opens a PR: D-upstream-reporting); otherwise it prepares a sanitized report and sends it to GitHub only with the operator's acceptance (B-upstream-surfaces). A GitHub workflow in the ddflow repository triages incoming reports (duplicate, needs-info, accepted) and accepted ones are imported into the ddflow queue as PROPOSED tasks. (3) KEEP WORK ACTIVE: at the end of a phase and when the ready queue is empty, ddflow runs a retro pass and (if budget remains and the job is enabled) a discovery pass that files capped, deduplicated PROPOSALS for the software the user builds, linked to goals; proposals never become tasks without the operator (B-prop-model). All three are periodic passes declared as data (config), with caps, a budget and a kill switch (AP-kill), and extend the goals-managed self product and project management (P-goals, P-autopilot).

data.text:
You are a code reviewer. Review the code changes shown below.

Return only the final review. Do NOT narrate your process, mention files you opened, or describe intermediate checks.
If you use tools while reviewing, finish all tool use before emitting the final review, and put the final review only after the last tool call.
Do NOT build the project, run the test suite, or execute the code while reviewing. You may read other files in the repository to verify claims made by the diff. If the diff references a file, package, function, or symbol that is not present in the diff itself, check whether it exists in the repo before asserting it doesn't.

## Output Format

- If you find issues, start immediately with `## Review Findings` and list only the findings:
  - **Severity**: High/Medium/Low
  - **Location**: File and line number where possible
  - **Problem**: Concise description of the issue
  - **Fix**: Brief suggested fix
- Separate multiple findings with `---` on its own line.
- After the findings, add `## Summary` with a single sentence summarizing the change.
- If you find no issues, start immediately with `No issues found.` and then add `Summary: <one sentence>`.

Do not include any front matter such as "Reviewing the diff..." or "I'm checking...".

## Review Criteria

1. **Bugs**: Logic errors, off-by-one errors, null/undefined issues, race conditions.
2. **Security**: Injection vulnerabilities, auth issues, data exposure.
3. **Testing gaps**: Missing unit tests, edge cases, e2e/integration gaps.
4. **Regressions**: Changes that might break existing functionality.
5. **Code quality**: Duplication, overly complex logic, unclear naming.

Do not review the commit message. Focus only on the code changes in the diff.

IMPORTANT: You are being invoked by roborev to perform this review directly. Do NOT use any external skills, slash commands, or CLI tools (such as "roborev review") to delegate this task. Perform the review yourself by analyzing the diff provided below.

Return only the final review content. Do NOT include process narration, progress updates, or front matter such as "Reviewing the diff..." or "I'm checking...".
If you use tools while reviewing, finish all tool use before emitting the final review, and put the final review only after the last tool call.

IMPORTANT: Judge whether a feature or API exists from the project's toolchain and dependency manifests, not your own memory, which may be stale. This cuts both ways: do not flag valid recent features as broken, and do not miss calls to APIs that genuinely do not exist for the project's versions.

Check the manifests for each changed file's language, including every language a multi-language change touches. Common ones:

- Go: go.mod / go.sum.
- TypeScript / JavaScript: package.json, a lockfile (yarn.lock, package-lock.json, pnpm-lock.yaml), tsconfig.json.
- Python: pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, uv/pixi lockfiles.
- Other languages: the equivalent manifests (Cargo.toml, pom.xml, build.gradle, Gemfile).

Current date: 2026-10-19 (UTC)

## Project Guidelines

These guidelines supplement the default review criteria and may add repo-specific expectations or constraints.

This repo (ddflow) is a work-queue kernel and MCP server for AI coding agents. It is event-sourced: an append-only JSONL log is the sole source of truth and everything else is a deterministic projection. Always state whether a finding is CONFIRMED (you traced or reproduced it) or THEORETICAL.

Prioritise the bug classes this project has actually shipped and then found, in rough order of how often they were real:

1. Vacuous pass — a check that cannot fail. A gate satisfied by an assertion with no evidence; `all()` over an empty collection; a test that passes with the feature disabled; a tool that exits 0 while reporting it could not run. This is the defining class here: "unavailable" must NEVER render as "success", and "nobody looked" must never render as "no".
2. Three-valued collapse — a tri-state (yes / no / could-not-tell) flattened into a boolean. Timeouts and spawn failures reported as absence; a probe that never ran cached as a negative result.
3. Silent-knob-drop — a config field accepted and never read, or dropped one layer down. Also a knob whose value is validated but discarded.
4. Duplicate-then-drift — the same quantity or logic defined twice, one shadowing the other. A dead fallback branch nothing executes, which therefore cannot be caught drifting. A top-level name defined twice in one module.
5. Metadata-key-vs-field — provenance carried as prose in a free-text body instead of a structured field, forcing a regex to recover it.
6. Projection drops a field — an event handler that silently discards keys the writer recorded, so the fold loses data the log still has.
7. Unreachable state used as a criterion — judging something by a status it can never attain (e.g. asking whether a command-line tool is "registered" as an MCP server).
8. Exit-code semantics — this project's vocabulary is 0 healthy, 1 failure, 2 could-not-run/nothing, 3 coordination refused. Collapsing 2 into 0 is a bug, always.
9. Concurrency — `fcntl.flock` is per open-file-description, so a second lock on one file in one process deadlocks against itself. Check-then-act outside a transaction. A lock held across an O(all-events) read. Process-global state (`sys.stdout`) swapped per call in something that may become reentrant.
10. Identity and attribution — anything that assumes one agent per process, per tree, or per connection. Several agents sharing a derived identity is a correctness bug, not a cosmetic one: reviewer independence is a comparison of agent against author.
11. Torn-tail resume — half-written state on restart; a non-atomic write with a fixed temp filename.
12. CLI/MCP divergence — the two surfaces are meant to be parity-tested. A capability on one and not the other, or the same operation encoded differently on each.

Also flag, specifically: a docstring that promises behaviour the code does not implement (this project has shipped that twice), and any source change that arrives without a runnable regression test demonstrating the defect.

to understand ongoing work and to check if the current commit addresses previous feedback.

**Important:** Reviews may include responses from developers. Pay attention to these responses -
they may indicate known issues that should be ignored, explain why certain patterns exist,
or provide context that affects how you should evaluate similar code in the current commit.

+"""Document types in ``ddflow docs check`` (B-dt-validate): the ``doctype`` finding family.
+
+Every tracked document that the check covers (``check_paths``, else the document globs minus
+the excluded and generated files, as for every other family) and that a type's ``path`` or
+``pattern`` names is validated against that type (shipped types, then
+`.ddflow/doctypes/*.toml`). A type that cannot be read, or a lint command that cannot run, is ``unavailable`` with the reason -- never a clean report. A type's
+``[doctype.validate] lint_command`` (e.g. ``vale {path}``) runs once per document, but only for
+a shipped type: a command in a project-added type stays inert until it is approved, said in
+``not_configured`` (declared, not asked for by the operator, so it does not poison the report).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import shlex
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath
+from string import Formatter
+from typing import Any
+
+from ..config import Config
+from .cmdrunner import CommandRunner, Declared
+from .docscheck import _tree
+from .docscheck_types import Finding
+from .docsync import glob_regex
+from .doctypes import spec
+from .doctypes.validate import validate
+
+PROJECT_DIR = ".ddflow/doctypes"
+
+
+def type_glob(dt: spec.DocType) -> str:
+    """The glob of the documents of ``dt``: a collection's placeholders become ``*``."""
+    if not dt.multi:
+        return dt.path
+    return "".join(
+        lit + ("*" if field is not None else "")
+        for lit, field, _, _ in Formatter().parse(dt.pattern)
+    )
+
+
+def types_of(repo: Path) -> list[spec.DocType]:
+    layers = [
+        spec.read_layer("shipped", spec.SHIPPED_DIR),
+        spec.read_layer("project", repo / PROJECT_DIR),
+    ]
+    return spec.registry(layers).values_list()
+
+
+def _lint(repo: Path, cfg: Config, dt: spec.DocType, path: str, check: Any) -> Iterable[Finding]:
+    line = str(dt.validate.get("lint_command", "")).strip().replace("{path}", shlex.quote(path))
+    key = f"lint:{dt.name}"
+    if not line:
+        return []
+    if not dt.source.startswith("shipped/"):
+        check.not_configured[key] = (
+            f"{dt.name}: a lint command in a project-added type is inert until approved"
+        )
+        return []
+    run = CommandRunner().run(
+        Declared(line, f"doctype {dt.name} lint_command"),
+        cwd=repo,
+        timeout_s=cfg.docs.command_timeout_s,
+        merge_stderr=True,
+    )
+    if not run.ran:
+        check.unavailable[key] = f"`{line}` did not run: {run.reason}"
+        return []
+    return (
+        [Finding("doctype", path, 0, "lint", f"exit {run.code}: {run.output.strip()}")]
+        if run.code
+        else []
+    )
+
+
+def check_doctypes(repo: Path, cfg: Config, check: Any, *, run_commands: bool = True) -> None:
+    """Add the ``doctype`` findings of every document that has a type to ``check``."""
+    report = check.report
+    try:
+        types = types_of(repo)
+    except (spec.DocTypeError, OSError) as exc:
+        check.unavailable["doctypes"] = str(exc)
+        return
+    tree = _tree(repo)
+    have = set(tree)
+    checked = set(report.checked.get("docs", []))  # the documents this check covers, no others
+    dirs = {str(p) for f in tree for p in PurePosixPath(f).parents}
+
+    def read(path: str) -> str | None:
+        """The text of a tracked file; "" for a tracked directory (a link to it resolves)."""
+        if path in have:
+            return (repo / path).read_text("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        return "" if path.rstrip("/") in dirs else None
+
+    count = 0
+    for dt in types:
+        rx = glob_regex(type_glob(dt))
+        for path in (p for p in tree if p in checked and rx.fullmatch(p)):
+            try:
+                text = read(path)
+                report.findings += validate(dt, text or "", path, read=read)
+            except OSError as exc:
+                check.unavailable["doctypes"] = f"{path}: {exc}"
+                continue
+            count += 1
+            if run_commands:
+                report.findings += _lint(repo, cfg, dt, path, check)
+            elif dt.validate.get("lint_command") and dt.source.startswith("shipped/"):
+                check.unavailable[f"lint:{dt.name}"] = "commands are off for this check"
+            elif dt.validate.get("lint_command"):
+                check.not_configured[f"lint:{dt.name}"] = (
+                    f"{dt.name}: a lint command in a project-added type is inert until approved"
+                )
+    report.checked["doctypes"] = count

+"""A document's structure, read with the standard library only (B-dt-validate).
+
+``parse(text)`` returns a `Doc`: the YAML front matter (a safe subset: ``key: value`` scalars,
+inline ``[a, b]`` lists, and ``- item`` block lists), the headings, and for each heading the
+section it opens -- its body up to the next heading of the same or a higher level -- with the
+code blocks, tables, list items and links in it. Fenced code is never read as prose or
+structure. Pure: reads text, never the tree.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any
+
+from ..docscheck import _LINK, _REFDEF  # the reference check's own grammar of a link
+from ..docscheck_md import SPAN, lines
+
+_ATX = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")
+_ITEM = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])\s+(.*\S)")
+_DELIM = re.compile(r"^\s*\|?\s*:?-{2,}:?\s*(\|\s*:?-{2,}:?\s*)*\|?\s*$")
+_FENCE_RUN = re.compile(r"^\s*(`{3,}|~{3,})\s*([\w+-]*)")
+_KEY = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z_][\w-]*)\s*:\s*(.*)$")
+_INT = re.compile(r"^-?\d+$")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Heading:
+    level: int
+    text: str
+    line: int
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Part:
+    heading: Heading
+    end: int  #: the last line of the section
+    body: str = ""  #: its prose lines (code blocks left out), joined
+    code_langs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  #: one entry per fenced block
+    tables: int = 0
+    items: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  #: list item texts
+    links: list[tuple[int, str]] = field(default_factory=list)  #: (line, target)
+
+    @property
+    def words(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.body.split())
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Doc:
+    front: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    front_error: str = ""  #: why the front matter could not be read, or ""
+    front_line: int = 0  #: the line after the front matter (1 when there is none)
+    headings: list[Heading] = field(default_factory=list)
+    parts: list[Part] = field(default_factory=list)
+    whole: Part = field(
+        default_factory=lambda: Part(Heading(0, "", 0), 0)
+    )  #: the document as one part
+    text: str = ""
+
+
+def _scalar(raw: str) -> Any:
+    v = raw.strip()
+    if len(v) > 1 and v[0] == v[-1] and v[0] in "\"'":
+        return v[1:-1]
+    low = v.lower()
+    if low in ("true", "false"):
+        return low == "true"
+    if low in ("null", "~", ""):
+        return None
+    return int(v) if _INT.match(v) else v
+
+
+def _flow(raw: str) -> Any:
+    v = raw.strip()
+    if v.startswith("[") and v.endswith("]"):
+        return [_scalar(p) for p in v[1:-1].split(",") if p.strip()]
+    return _scalar(v)
+
+
+def front_matter(text: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str, int]:
+    """(mapping, error, first line after the block). No block is ({}, "", 1)."""
+    rows = text.splitlines()
+    if not rows or rows[0].strip() != "---":
+        return {}, "", 1
+    close = next((i for i in range(1, len(rows)) if rows[i].strip() in ("---", "...")), 0)
+    if not close:
+        return {}, "front matter is opened with --- but never closed", 1
+    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
+    key = ""
+    for n, row in enumerate(rows[1:close], 2):
+        if not row.strip() or row.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        item = re.match(r"^\s+-\s+(.*)$", row) or re.match(r"^-\s+(.*)$", row)
+        if item and key and isinstance(out.get(key), list):
+            out[key].append(_scalar(item.group(1)))
+            continue
+        m = _KEY.match(row)
+        if not m:
+            return out, f"line {n}: not a `key: value` pair in the front matter", close + 2
+        key, val = m.group(1), m.group(2)
+        out[key] = [] if val.strip() == "" else _flow(val)
+    return out, "", close + 2
+
+
+def parse(text: str) -> Doc:
+    front, err, first = front_matter(text)
+    doc = Doc(front, err, first, text=text)
+    total = len(text.splitlines())
+    doc.whole = Part(Heading(0, "", first - 1), total)
+    live: list[Part] = [doc.whole]  # parts still open: each runs to a heading at or above it
+    fence: tuple[str, int] | None = None  # the open code block's fence character and length
+    prev = ""
+    for n, line, code in lines(text):
+        if n < first:
+            continue
+        if code:
+            m = _FENCE_RUN.match(line)
+            if fence is None:
+                fence = (m.group(1)[0], len(m.group(1))) if m else ("`", 3)
+                for s in live:
+                    s.code_langs.append(m.group(2) if m else "")
+            elif m and m.group(1)[0] == fence[0] and len(m.group(1)) >= fence[1]:
+                fence = fence if line.strip() != m.group(1) else None  # a closer has no info string
+            prev = line
+            continue
+        fence = None
+        if h := _ATX.match(line):
+            head = Heading(len(h.group(1)), h.group(2), n)
+            for s in [s for s in live if s.heading.level >= head.level]:
+                s.end = n - 1
+                live.remove(s)
+            sec = Part(head, total)
+            live.append(sec)
+            doc.parts.append(sec)
+            doc.headings.append(head)
+        else:
+            _read(live, line, prev, n)
+        prev = line
+    return doc
+
+
+def _targets(line: str) -> list[str]:
+    """The link targets on one line, as the reference link check reads them: inline and image
+    links outside code spans, and a reference definition."""
+    masked = SPAN.sub(lambda c: " " * len(c.group(0)), line)
+    found = [m.group(1) for m in _LINK.finditer(masked)]
+    return found + ([d.group(1)] if (d := _REFDEF.match(masked)) else [])
+
+
+def _read(live: list[Part], line: str, prev: str, n: int) -> None:
+    item = _ITEM.match(line)
+    table = bool("|" in line and "|" in prev and _DELIM.match(line))
+    links = [(n, t) for t in _targets(line)]
+    for s in live:
+        s.body += ("\n" if s.body else "") + line
+        s.tables += table
+        if item:
+            s.items.append(item.group(1))
+        s.links += links

+"""Scored rubrics a document type can name: a list of yes/no checks, scored by the share met.
+
+Shipped: ``security-policy`` (after OpenSSF Scorecard: contact, disclosure terms, response
+time), ``keep-a-changelog`` and ``madr``. A rubric is a function of the parsed document that
+returns ``(check, passed)`` pairs; a new one is registered in `RUBRICS`.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from ...core.registry import Registry
+from . import mdparse
+
+Rubric = Callable[[mdparse.Doc], list[tuple[str, bool]]]
+RUBRICS: Registry[tuple[str, Rubric]] = Registry("rubric", key=lambda r: r[0])
+
+
+def _has(doc: mdparse.Doc, rx: str) -> bool:
+    return re.search(rx, doc.text, re.I) is not None
+
+
+def _heading(doc: mdparse.Doc, rx: str) -> bool:
+    return any(re.search(rx, h.text, re.I) for h in doc.headings)
+
+
+def security_policy(doc: mdparse.Doc) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:
+    return [
+        ("a contact to report to", _has(doc, r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.-]+|https?://\S+")),
+        ("disclosure terms", _has(doc, r"disclos|coordinated|responsible")),
+        (
+            "a response time",
+            _has(doc, r"(respon|acknowledg)[^.\n]*\b\d+\s*(business\s+)?(hours?|days?|weeks?)\b"),
+        ),
+    ]
+
+
+def keep_a_changelog(doc: mdparse.Doc) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:
+    kinds = ("Added", "Changed", "Deprecated", "Removed", "Fixed", "Security")
+    return [
+        ("an Unreleased section", _heading(doc, r"^\[?unreleased\]?$")),
+        (
+            "a dated version heading",
+            _heading(doc, r"^\[?v?\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?\S*\]?\s*[-\u2013]\s*\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}"),
+        ),
+        ("change-type subsections", any(_heading(doc, rf"^{k}$") for k in kinds)),
+    ]
+
+
+def madr(doc: mdparse.Doc) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:
+    return [
+        ("a title", any(h.level == 1 for h in doc.headings)),
+        ("a problem statement", _heading(doc, r"context and problem statement")),
+        ("considered options", _heading(doc, r"considered options")),
+        ("a decision outcome", _heading(doc, r"decision outcome")),
+        ("a status in the front matter", "status" in doc.front),
+    ]
+
+
+for _name, _fn in (
+    ("security-policy", security_policy),
+    ("keep-a-changelog", keep_a_changelog),
+    ("madr", madr),
+):
+    RUBRICS.register((_name, _fn))

+"""Validate rules about what a section says: text, size, code, tables, lists, links."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import posixpath
+import re
+from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
+from typing import Any
+from urllib.parse import unquote
+
+from ..docscheck_md import anchors_of
+from ..docscheck_types import Finding
+from .validate import Ctx, regex, rule
+
+_ASK = re.compile(r"<!--\s*ask\b|\{\{\s*ask\b|\[ASK\b", re.I)
+_EXTERNAL = re.compile(r"^(?:[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:|//)", re.I)
+
+
+def _required(kind: str, ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    rx, bad = regex(ctx, r)
+    yield from bad
+    if rx and ctx.scope(r) and not rx.search("\n".join(t for _, t in ctx.prose(r))):
+        yield ctx.finding(kind, 1, f"no text matches /{rx.pattern}/", r)
+
+
+@rule("required_text", "regex")
+def required_text(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    yield from _required("required_text", ctx, r)
+
+
+@rule("pattern", "regex")
+def pattern(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """The document (or section) contains text matching ``regex``."""
+    yield from _required("pattern", ctx, r)
+
+
+@rule("forbidden_text", "regex")
+def forbidden_text(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    rx, bad = regex(ctx, r)
+    yield from bad
+    for n, line in ctx.prose(r) if rx else []:
+        if rx.search(line):
+            yield ctx.finding("forbidden_text", n, f"text matching /{rx.pattern}/", r)
+
+
+@rule("forbidden_whole_text", "regex")
+def forbidden_whole_text(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """A vacuous assertion: a regex over the whole prose of the scope, across lines."""
+    rx, bad = regex(ctx, r)
+    yield from bad
+    rows = ctx.prose(r) if rx else []
+    m = rx.search("\n".join(t for _, t in rows)) if rx else None
+    if m and rows:
+        line = rows[_row_at(rows, m.start())][0]
+        yield ctx.finding("forbidden_whole_text", line, f"text matching /{rx.pattern}/", r)
+
+
+def _row_at(rows: list[tuple[int, str]], offset: int) -> int:
+    """The index in ``rows`` of the line holding ``offset`` of their newline-joined text."""
+    pos = 0
+    for i, (_, t) in enumerate(rows):
+        pos += len(t) + 1
+        if offset < pos:
+            return i
+    return max(len(rows) - 1, 0)
+
+
+def _bound(kind: str, ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any], want_max: bool) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    limit = r.get("limit")
+    if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool):
+        yield ctx.finding(kind, 1, "limit must be an integer", r)
+    elif part := ctx.scope(r):
+        words, line = part.words, max(part.heading.line, 1)
+        if want_max and words > limit:
+            yield ctx.finding(kind, line, f"{words} words is over {limit}", r)
+        elif not want_max and words < limit:
+            yield ctx.finding(kind, line, f"{words} words is under {limit}", r)
+
+
+@rule("max_words", "limit")
+def max_words(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    yield from _bound("max_words", ctx, r, True)
+
+
+@rule("min_words", "limit")
+def min_words(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    yield from _bound("min_words", ctx, r, False)
+
+
+@rule("code_blocks", "lang", "min")
+def code_blocks(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    if part := ctx.scope(r):
+        want, need = r.get("lang"), r.get("min", 1)
+        if not isinstance(need, int) or isinstance(need, bool):
+            yield ctx.finding("code_blocks", 1, "min must be an integer", r)
+            return
+        have = [x for x in part.code_langs if not want or x == want]
+        if len(have) < need:
+            lang = f" in {want}" if want else ""
+            yield ctx.finding(
+                "code_blocks",
+                max(part.heading.line, 1),
+                f"{len(have)} code block(s){lang}; wants {need}",
+                r,
+            )
+
+
+@rule("has_table")
+def has_table(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    if (part := ctx.scope(r)) and not part.tables:
+        yield ctx.finding("has_table", max(part.heading.line, 1), "no table", r)
+
+
+@rule("has_list")
+def has_list(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    if (part := ctx.scope(r)) and not part.items:
+        yield ctx.finding("has_list", max(part.heading.line, 1), "no list", r)
+
+
+@rule("each_item_matches", "regex")
+def each_item_matches(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """Every list item of the section matches ``regex`` (e.g. each expectation names its falsifier)."""
+    rx, bad = regex(ctx, r)
+    yield from bad
+    part = ctx.scope(r)
+    if rx and part and not part.items:
+        yield ctx.finding(
+            "each_item_matches", max(part.heading.line, 1), "no list items to match", r
+        )
+    for item in part.items if rx and part else []:
+        if not rx.search(item):
+            yield ctx.finding(
+                "each_item_matches",
+                part.heading.line,
+                f"item {item[:60]!r} does not match /{rx.pattern}/",
+                r,
+            )
+
+
+@rule("no_ask_placeholder")
+def no_ask_placeholder(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """No question to the user is left open (an ``<!-- ask: ... -->`` marker, which a prose
+    check would skip as code or comment, so every line of the scope is read)."""
+    if part := ctx.scope(r):
+        for n, line in enumerate(ctx.doc.text.splitlines(), 1):
+            if part.heading.line <= n <= part.end and _ASK.search(line):
+                yield ctx.finding("no_ask_placeholder", n, "an open ask placeholder", r)
+
+
+@rule("links_resolve")
+def links_resolve(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """Local links in the scope reach a tracked file and, when they name one, a heading."""
+    if (part := ctx.scope(r)) is None:
+        return
+    if ctx.read is None:
+        yield ctx.finding("links_resolve", 1, "cannot tell: no way to read the tree", r)
+        return
+    for n, url in part.links:
+        if _EXTERNAL.match(url):
+            continue
+        base, _, frag = url.partition("#")
+        target, frag = unquote(base.partition("?")[0]), unquote(frag)
+        if target.startswith("/"):  # root-relative, as the reference check reads it
+            dest = posixpath.normpath(target.lstrip("/"))
+        else:
+            dest = (
+                posixpath.normpath(posixpath.join(posixpath.dirname(ctx.path), target))
+                if target
+                else ctx.path
+            )
+        text = ctx.doc.text if not target else ctx.read(dest)
+        if text is None:
+            yield ctx.finding("links_resolve", n, f"{url}: {dest} is not in the tree", r)
+        elif (
+            frag
+            and dest.lower().endswith((".md", ".markdown"))
+            and frag.lower() not in anchors_of(text)
+        ):
+            yield ctx.finding("links_resolve", n, f"{url}: no heading #{frag} in {dest}", r)

+"""Validate rules about the front matter: a schema, drafts, and review dates."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from ...core import clock
+from ..docscheck_types import Finding
+from .validate import Ctx, rule
+
+_TYPES: dict[str, type | tuple[type, ...]] = {
+    "string": str,
+    "integer": int,
+    "boolean": bool,
+    "array": list,
+    "number": (int, float),
+    "object": dict,
+    "null": type(None),
+}
+DRAFT_STATES = ("draft", "proposed", "wip")
+
+
+def _type_ok(value: Any, name: str) -> bool:
+    if name in ("integer", "number") and isinstance(value, bool):
+        return False
+    return isinstance(value, _TYPES[name])
+
+
+def schema_problems(front: Mapping[str, Any], schema: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[str]:
+    """What a JSON-Schema subset (``required``, ``properties`` with ``type`` ``enum``
+    ``pattern``) finds wrong with ``front``."""
+    required, props = schema.get("required", []), schema.get("properties", {})
+    if not isinstance(required, list) or not isinstance(props, dict):
+        raise TypeError("required must be a list and properties a table")
+    for key in required:
+        if key not in front:
+            yield f"{key!r} is required"
+    for key, spec in props.items():
+        if key not in front:
+            continue
+        v = front[key]
+        if not isinstance(spec, dict):
+            yield f"{key!r}: the property schema must be a table"
+            continue
+        if "type" in spec and spec["type"] not in _TYPES:
+            yield f"{key!r}: the schema type {spec['type']!r} is not supported ({', '.join(_TYPES)})"
+        elif "type" in spec and not _type_ok(v, spec["type"]):
+            yield f"{key!r} must be {spec['type']}"
+        elif "enum" in spec and v not in spec["enum"]:
+            yield f"{key!r} is {v!r}; one of {', '.join(map(str, spec['enum']))}"
+        elif "pattern" in spec and not re.search(spec["pattern"], str(v)):
+            yield f"{key!r} does not match /{spec['pattern']}/"
+
+
+@rule("front_matter", "schema", section=False)
+def front_matter(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    schema = r.get("schema")
+    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
+        yield ctx.finding("front_matter", 1, "schema must be a table", r)
+        return
+    try:
+        for problem in schema_problems(ctx.doc.front, schema):
+            yield ctx.finding("front_matter", 1, problem, r)
+    except (re.error, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
+        yield ctx.finding("front_matter", 1, f"the schema cannot be applied: {exc}", r)
+
+
+@rule("no_draft", section=False)
+def no_draft(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """A document the type calls accepted is not still a draft."""
+    f = ctx.doc.front
+    if f.get("draft") is True or str(f.get("status", "")).strip().casefold() in DRAFT_STATES:
+        yield ctx.finding("no_draft", 1, "the front matter marks this document a draft", r)
+
+
+@rule("not_expired", section=False)
+def not_expired(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """``review_by`` (an ISO date) is not in the past."""
+    raw = ctx.doc.front.get("review_by")
+    if raw is None:
+        return
+    try:
+        due = clock.parse_date(str(raw))
+    except ValueError:
+        yield ctx.finding("not_expired", 1, f"review_by {raw!r} is not an ISO date", r)
+        return
+    if due < ctx.today:
+        yield ctx.finding("not_expired", 1, f"review_by {due} has passed", r)

+"""The ``rubric`` validate rule: a named scored rubric, with a minimum score."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from ..docscheck_types import Finding
+from .rubrics import RUBRICS
+from .validate import Ctx, rule
+
+
+@rule("rubric", "name", "min_score", section=False)
+def rubric(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    name, floor = r.get("name"), r.get("min_score", 1.0)
+    if not isinstance(name, str) or name not in RUBRICS:
+        yield ctx.finding("rubric", 1, f"unknown rubric {name!r}. Known: {', '.join(RUBRICS)}", r)
+        return
+    if not isinstance(floor, (int, float)) or isinstance(floor, bool):
+        yield ctx.finding("rubric", 1, "min_score must be a number", r)
+        return
+    checks = RUBRICS[name][1](ctx.doc)
+    met = sum(ok for _, ok in checks)
+    if checks and met / len(checks) < floor:
+        miss = ", ".join(c for c, ok in checks if not ok)
+        yield ctx.finding("rubric", 1, f"{name} scored {met}/{len(checks)}; missing {miss}", r)

+"""Validate rules about a document's shape: sections, heading order and levels, size."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Iterator, Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from ..docscheck_types import Finding
+from .validate import Ctx, rule
+
+
+@rule("required_sections")
+def required_sections(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """Each section the type marks ``required`` is in the document, at its heading level."""
+    for sec in ctx.dt.sections:
+        if not sec.required or not sec.heading or r.get("section", sec.id) != sec.id:
+            continue
+        part = ctx.found[sec.id]
+        if part is None:
+            yield ctx.finding("required_sections", 1, f"missing section {sec.heading!r}", r)
+        elif part.heading.level != sec.level:
+            yield ctx.finding(
+                "required_sections",
+                part.heading.line,
+                f"{sec.heading!r} is a level {part.heading.level} heading; the type wants {sec.level}",
+                r,
+            )
+
+
+@rule("heading_order", section=False)
+def heading_order(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """The type's sections that are present follow its order."""
+    last = None
+    for sec in ctx.dt.sections:
+        part = ctx.found.get(sec.id)
+        if part is None:
+            continue
+        if last is not None and part.heading.line < last.heading.line:
+            yield ctx.finding(
+                "heading_order",
+                part.heading.line,
+                f"{sec.heading!r} comes before {last.heading.text!r}; the type orders it after",
+                r,
+            )
+        else:
+            last = part
+
+
+@rule("no_skipped_levels", section=False)
+def no_skipped_levels(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """A heading is at most one level deeper than the one before it."""
+    prev = 0
+    for h in ctx.doc.headings:
+        if prev and h.level > prev + 1:
+            yield ctx.finding(
+                "no_skipped_levels", h.line, f"{h.text!r} skips from level {prev} to {h.level}", r
+            )
+        prev = h.level
+
+
+@rule("unique_headings", section=False)
+def unique_headings(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    """No two headings of the same level read the same."""
+    seen: dict[tuple[int, str], int] = {}
+    for h in ctx.doc.headings:
+        key = (h.level, h.text.casefold())
+        if key in seen:
+            yield ctx.finding(
+                "unique_headings", h.line, f"{h.text!r} repeats the heading on line {seen[key]}", r
+            )
+        seen.setdefault(key, h.line)
+
+
+@rule("max_bytes", "limit", section=False)
+def max_bytes(ctx: Ctx, r: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Iterator[Finding]:
+    size, limit = len(ctx.doc.text.encode()), r.get("limit")
+    if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool):
+        yield ctx.finding("max_bytes", 1, "limit must be an integer", r)
+    elif size > limit:
+        yield ctx.finding("max_bytes", 1, f"{size} bytes is over the limit of {limit}", r)

index 000000000..77a78cffc
--- /dev/null
+++ b/ddflow/services/doctypes/validate.py
@@ -0,0 +1,135 @@
+"""Validate a document against its type (B-dt-validate): the engine.
+
+``validate(dt, text, path)`` reads the document once (`mdparse`), finds the type's sections in it,
+and runs each ``[[doctype.validate.rules]]`` entry of the type. A rule kind is a function in a
+``rule_*.py`` file of this package that registers itself with `rule` -- a new kind is a new file,
+and `spec.RULE_KINDS` (which finds those files) lists it, so a descriptor can name it. A rule
+that cannot be applied (a bad regex, a link target it cannot read) is a finding saying so,
+never silence. Findings are the docs check's `Finding` of kind ``doctype``.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import date
+from typing import Any
+
+from ...core import clock
+from ..docscheck_md import lines
+from ..docscheck_types import Finding
+from . import mdparse
+from .spec import RULE_KINDS, DocType, RuleKind
+
+Read = Callable[[str], "str | None"]
+Check = Callable[["Ctx", Mapping[str, Any]], Iterable[Finding]]
+
+#: Keys every rule kind may carry: the message that replaces its default. A kind that judges
+#: one section also takes ``section``; one that judges the whole document (`section=False`)
+#: refuses it at load rather than ignoring it.
+COMMON_KEYS = frozenset({"message"})
+
+
+def rule(name: str, *keys: str, section: bool = True) -> Callable[[Check], Check]:
+    """Register ``fn`` as the check of the validate rule kind ``name`` (with these keys)."""
+
+    def deco(fn: Check) -> Check:
+        RULE_KINDS.register(
+            RuleKind(name, COMMON_KEYS | frozenset(keys) | ({"section"} if section else set()), fn)
+        )
+        return fn
+
+    return deco
+
+
+@dataclass
+class Ctx:
+    """One document under check: its type, structure, path, and what a rule may look up."""
+
+    dt: DocType
+    doc: mdparse.Doc
+    path: str
+    #: Text of a tracked file; "" for a tracked directory; None when it is not tracked.
+    read: Read | None = None
+    today: date = field(default_factory=lambda: clock.now_utc().date())
+    found: dict[str, mdparse.Part | None] = field(default_factory=dict)
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        for sec in self.dt.sections:
+            self.found[sec.id] = (
+                self._locate(sec.heading, sec.match, sec.level) if sec.heading else None
+            )
+
+    def _locate(self, heading: str, match: str, level: int) -> mdparse.Part | None:
+        try:
+            rx = (
+                re.compile(heading)
+                if match == "regex"
+                else re.compile(re.escape(heading), re.IGNORECASE)
+            )
+        except re.error:
+            return None  # `spec` refuses a bad heading regex at load; a hand-built type reads as absent
+        hits = [p for p in self.doc.parts if rx.fullmatch(p.heading.text)]
+        return next((p for p in hits if p.heading.level == level), hits[0] if hits else None)
+
+    def finding(self, rule_kind: str, line: int, detail: str, rule_: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Finding:
+        ref = rule_kind + (f":{rule_['section']}" if rule_.get("section") else "")
+        return Finding("doctype", self.path, line, ref, str(rule_.get("message") or detail))
+
+    def scope(self, rule_: Mapping[str, Any]) -> mdparse.Part | None:
+        """The part a rule judges: its section, or the whole document when it names none.
+        None when it names a section the document lacks: a required one is reported by
+        `required_sections`, an optional one has nothing to judge."""
+        sid = rule_.get("section")
+        return self.found.get(sid) if sid else self.doc.whole
+
+    def prose(self, rule_: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
+        """(line number, line) of the prose in a rule's scope; fenced code is left out."""
+        part = self.scope(rule_)
+        if part is None:
+            return []
+        return [
+            (n, ln)
+            for n, ln, code in lines(self.doc.text)
+            if part.heading.line < n <= part.end and not code
+        ]
+
+
+def regex(
+    ctx: Ctx, rule_: Mapping[str, Any], key: str = "regex"
+) -> tuple[re.Pattern | None, list[Finding]]:
+    """The compiled ``rule_[key]``, or a finding saying the rule cannot be applied."""
+    if not str(rule_.get(key, "")):
+        return None, [ctx.finding(str(rule_["kind"]), 1, f"{key} is required", rule_)]
+    try:
+        return re.compile(str(rule_[key]), re.M), []
+    except re.error as exc:
+        return None, [
+            ctx.finding(str(rule_["kind"]), 1, f"{key} is not a regular expression: {exc}", rule_)
+        ]
+
+
+def validate(
+    dt: DocType, text: str, path: str, *, read: Read | None = None, today: date | None = None
+) -> list[Finding]:
+    """Every finding of ``dt``'s rules against ``text``, in line order."""
+    ctx = Ctx(dt, mdparse.parse(text), path, read, today or clock.now_utc().date())
+    out: list[Finding] = []
+    if ctx.doc.front_error:
+        out.append(Finding("doctype", path, 1, "front_matter", ctx.doc.front_error))
+    for r in dt.validate.get("rules", []):
+        try:
+            kind = RULE_KINDS[r["kind"]]
+        except KeyError as exc:
+            out.append(Finding("doctype", path, 1, str(r.get("kind")), str(exc)))
+            continue
+        if kind.check is None:
+            out.append(Finding("doctype", path, 1, kind.name, "the rule kind has no check"))
+            continue
+        sec = r.get("section")
+        if sec is not None and (not isinstance(sec, str) or sec not in ctx.found):
+            out.append(ctx.finding(kind.name, 1, f"unknown section {sec!r}", r))
+            continue
+        out += kind.check(ctx, r)
+    return sorted(out, key=lambda f: (f.line, f.ref, f.detail))

+"""B-dt-validate: a document checked against its type, rule kind by rule kind."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from datetime import date
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
+
+from ddflow import api
+from ddflow.services.doctypes import mdparse, spec
+from ddflow.services.doctypes.rubrics import RUBRICS
+from ddflow.services.doctypes.validate import validate
+
+FIRST_LINE, LAST_LINE = 7, 18
+ADR = (
+    "# 1. Use X\n\n## Status\n\nAccepted\n\n## Context\n\nWhy.\n\n## Decision\n\nWe do.\n\n"
+    "## Consequences\n\nFine.\n"
+)
+
+
+def dtype(rules: str, sections: str = "") -> spec.DocType:
+    return spec.parse(
+        '[doctype]\nname = "t"\npath = "T.md"\n'
+        + sections
+        + f"[doctype.validate]\nrules = [{rules}]\n"
+    )
+
+
+def sec(sid: str, heading: str, **kw) -> str:
+    extra = "".join(f"{k} = {v}\n" for k, v in kw.items())
+    return f'[[doctype.section]]\nid = "{sid}"\nheading = "{heading}"\n{extra}'
+
+
+def found(dt, text, **kw) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
+    return [(f.ref, f.line) for f in validate(dt, text, "T.md", **kw)]
+
+
+def test_parser_reads_front_matter_parts_and_skips_code():
+    d = mdparse.parse(
+        "---\nstatus: draft\ntags: [a, b]\nowners:\n  - x\n---\n# T\n\n## Ctx\nsee [l](a.md)\n- one\n"
+        "```py\n# not a heading\n```\n| a | b |\n|---|---|\n### Sub\nmore\n## Next\n"
+    )
+    assert d.front == {"status": "draft", "tags": ["a", "b"], "owners": ["x"]}
+    assert d.front_line == FIRST_LINE
+    assert [h.text for h in d.headings] == ["T", "Ctx", "Sub", "Next"]
+    ctx = d.parts[1]
+    assert ctx.code_langs == ["py"] and ctx.tables == 1 and ctx.items == ["one"]
+    assert ctx.links == [(10, "a.md")]
+    assert ctx.end == LAST_LINE
+
+
+def test_unclosed_front_matter_is_reported():
+    assert "never closed" in mdparse.parse("---\na: 1\n# T\n").front_error
+    assert [f.ref for f in validate(dtype(""), "---\na: 1\n", "T.md")] == ["front_matter"]
+
+
+def test_the_shipped_adr_passes_and_names_what_is_missing():
+    adr = spec.registry()["adr"]
+    assert validate(adr, ADR, "docs/adr/0001-x.md") == []
+    text = ADR.replace("## Decision\n\nWe do.\n\n", "")
+    assert found(adr, text) == [("required_sections", 1)]
+    swapped = (
+        ADR.replace("## Context", "## Zed")
+        .replace("## Decision", "## Context")
+        .replace("## Zed", "## Decision")
+    )
+    assert [r for r, _ in found(adr, swapped)] == ["heading_order"]
+
+
+def test_a_wrong_level_is_named():
+    dt = dtype('{ kind = "required_sections" }', sec("c", "Context", required="true"))
+    assert found(dt, "# Context\n") == [("required_sections", 1)]
+    assert found(dt, "## Context\n") == []
+

data.summary: argparse reports 'ambiguous option: --mutation could match --mutation-file, --mutation-old, --mutation-new'. The MCP tool takes one JSON 'mutation'; the CLI needs three flags. Two agents tripped on it. Either accept --mutation JSON on the CLI like MCP (parity) or say the three flags in the complete help and the gate text.
data.title: ddflow complete --mutation is an ambiguous abbreviation; briefs and docs say --mutation but the real flags are --mutation-file/--mutation-old/--mutation-new

data.summary: ddflow dupes takes no positional item id; the dedupe gate guidance says to search by operation and agents try 'ddflow dupes <id>' and get an argparse error. Accept an item id (scan that item's diff/title against the rest) or point the gate text at 'ddflow similar'.
data.title: ddflow dupes <item-id> is rejected although gate text and agents expect a per-item duplicate scan

data.alternatives: 5 rounds (rejected: later rounds find fewer defects; 4 covers a full round, a fix round and two follow-ups); keep 2 plus per-case grants (rejected: operator interrupts); on_exceed=warn (rejected: unlimited rounds).
data.context: Agents repeatedly hit the 2-round cap because each fix after a review changes the tree (B-triage-guard-compares-whole-tree), and each extra round cost the operator a question. Operator 2026-10-21: 'automate justified grantings to the rubber duck up to some sensible number, lets say 4 or 5, with just a report to the user'.
data.decision: [review].max_rounds = 4 for this project (was 2). Within the 4 rounds an agent needs no operator grant: every finding is triaged with a probe and a round is justified by a real finding or new code after the last round. Beyond 4 rounds, or a round that is not justified (no new code or finding), is the operator's. Agents report the rounds used per gate in their final report and complete lists passed-on-refutation gates; the operator reads the report and 'ddflow gate list --refuted'.
data.title: Review budget raised to 4 rounds per gate; justified extra rounds are automatic, reported not asked

data.summary: After the project review.max_rounds change landed on main (a77abbffa) the commit hook refused commits in running agents' worktrees ('stale_rules') and the only way past it was a real git merge main, after their last review round. A config knob change is not a rule change: the hook should compare the rules/decisions the agent was briefed on, not the whole .ddflow/config.toml, or allow commits that only touch files outside the changed rules. Related: B-triage-guard-compares-whole-tree.
data.title: Committing a .ddflow/config.toml change on main makes the stale_rules hook block every in-flight worktree until it merges main, which invalidates settled review rounds

data.summary: An agent passed the operator's words as the positional argument; that is parsed as the SESSION id and the command then reads the text from stdin, so it blocks. Refuse a positional that is not a session id (h-... form) with a pointer to --text, or when stdin is a tty/empty.
data.title: ddflow session prompt "<text>" hangs waiting on stdin: the positional is the session id, the text needs --text

data.summary: An agent with uncommitted work was refused a commit by stale_rules (main changed .ddflow/config.toml). git reset --hard is blocked by the forbidden_commands hook and git merge main refuses while the worktree is dirty, so the agent copied files aside, merged, and copied them back. The refusal text should name one supported way (e.g. 'ddflow sync' or 'git stash push -u -m <tag>' + merge + apply) or ddflow should offer 'ddflow sync --keep-local'. Related: B-stale-rules-hook-forces-main-merge.
data.title: After a stale_rules commit refusal the only way out was copying files aside: hard reset is hook-blocked and a plain merge refuses with local changes

Fixes bug B-stale-rules-escape-needs-file-copy: An agent with uncommitted work was refused a commit by stale_rules (main changed .ddflow/config.toml). git reset --hard is blocked by the forbidden_commands hook and git merge main refuses while the worktree is dirty, so the agent copied files aside, merged, and copied them back. The refusal text should name one supported way (e.g. 'ddflow sync' or 'git stash push -u -m <tag>' + merge + apply) or ddflow should offer 'ddflow sync --keep-local'. Related: B-stale-rules-hook-forces-main-merge.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B-stale-rules-escape-needs-file-copy --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B-stale-rules-escape-needs-file-copy --regression-test <test>` first).

data.body: Operator 2026-10-21 asked whether agents working in worktrees from the same branch are notified when a file is fixed and merged to main so they pull it and stay in sync. Today (verified): ddflow sync exists (DX-sync-command, done), the drift calculation is shared (DX-drift-core, done), and a PULL-style notice is planned (DX-drift-notice: drift rides on heartbeat, brief and hook context) with sync points claim/pre_review/pre_ci/pre_merge (DX-sync-points: deliberately not continuous, because syncing after every merge invalidates recorded gate results; with reviewed_paths from B-triage-guard-compares-whole-tree an unrelated main merge no longer invalidates a settled round, which makes cheaper syncing possible). Missing: a PUSH at merge time. Design: when ddflow_merge lands an item, compute the merged paths and, for every live item with a worktree, intersect them with (its changed files, its lazily leased files from DX-lease-lazy-acquire, the files its reviewed round covered); write a 'drift.relevant' event per affected item naming the paths and the commit, which surfaces on the item's next tool result footer / heartbeat / hook context (DX-drift-notice) and, for a waiting or idle agent, wakes it (DX-wake-waiters). Unrelated merges produce no notice. [sync].mode decides: off|notify|auto (auto = run ddflow sync when the worktree is clean and the merge touches none of the item's files)|require (the next gate refuses until synced when a relevant file changed). Tests: relevant merge notifies, unrelated merge is silent, auto syncs only when clean and disjoint.
data.title: On merge to main, tell the live items whose changed or leased files intersect the merge (relevant drift), and offer a clean ddflow sync

data.summary: Left unfixed in fix-B-stale-rules-escape-needs-file-copy (rubber_duck confirmed 2, roborev 3): (1) _drop ignores whether 'git stash store' succeeded when it stores a stranger's entry back, so that entry can be lost; (2) after 5 consecutive races the drop loop gives up, reports success and leaves a duplicate stash entry; (3) if 'git stash list' fails right after a successful push, _stash_find treats it as 'no entry', orphaning the user's stash with no restore and no note. All need races or git failures, but each is a real data-loss path in a command whose purpose is to protect uncommitted work. Fix: check the store result, report an incomplete drop, treat a failed list as unknown (restore by the tag, or refuse).
