chunk_findings.detail: `scope_to_diff` validates `since` with `W.rev(tree, since)` but then interpolates the original `since` directly into the shell command string: `command.replace(" --all-files", f" --from-ref {since} --to-ref HEAD", 1)`. If `since` is a ref name containing shell metacharacters (for example a Git ref such as `foo$(touch /tmp/pwn)` or `foo;touch /tmp/pwn`, which can be valid ref names), `W.rev` can resolve it, so the function returns a command like `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref foo$(touch /tmp/pwn) --to-ref HEAD`. chunk_findings.detail:
The test’s lint hook swallows non-“BAD found” grep failures. `SCRIPT` is `#!/bin/sh
if grep -q BAD "$@"; then exit 1; fi
exit 0
`, so it only exits 1 when `grep` exits 0 (marker found). If `grep` exits 2 because a passed file is missing/unreadable, or exits 127 because `grep` is not available, or misparses a filename beginning with `-` as an option, the `if` condition is false and the script falls through to `exit 0`. For example, `scripts/lint.sh deleted.py` returns 0 even though it could not check the file; a diff-scoped pre-commit run that passes a deleted or oddly named file could therefore see the hook “pass” when it did not actually lint the input.

chunk_findings.detail: `_read_list` returns `([], "")` for any successful JSON value that is not a list (and for a list whose entries are not dicts), not just for the documented `null` “no jobs for this repository” case. Given `roborev list --json --limit ...` exits 0 with stdout `{"error":"daemon unavailable"}` (or any non-list JSON such as `false`), the function gives an empty list and an empty failure note. A caller that relies on the note to distinguish “could not read the status” from “read succeeded and the job is absent” will see a successful empty list; `wait_job` can then report the job as vanished/unavailable rather than reporting that the status read failed. The function should return a non-empty note for non-list/non-null output if it is to preserve the “failed read has a note” contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:_read_list

chunk_findings.detail: The done path still can run past the caller’s `wait_s` bound. With `wait_s=1`, if the list poll sees `done` when about 0.1s remain, `allowance` is 0.1 but `max(1.0, allowance)` gives `_done` a full 1.0s allowance. `_done` then runs `roborev wait --job` with `max(1.0, 1.0)`; if that ask hangs it consumes 1.0s, and `roborev show --job` still receives `max(0.5, timeout - spent)`, i.e. another 0.5s. The call can therefore block for roughly 1.5s after the bound (and the poll cap can already add up to 1.0s when the remaining bound is below 1.0s). The previous fix shares one allowance, but the 1.0s/0.5s floors mean a bounded wait can still exceed `wait_s`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:wait_job / _done

chunk_findings.detail: The zero-bound path ignores the bound when choosing the poll timeout: `cap = _TIMEOUT_S if wait_s <= 0 else ...`. Given `wait_job(repo, 7, 0)` and a `roborev list --json` read that hangs, the call blocks for the whole module default `_TIMEOUT_S` (the incident’s default ask timeout was 100s) before the post-read `elapsed >= wait_s` check can return live. The earlier triage said the poll read is capped at the remaining bound with a 1.0s floor, but for `wait_s <= 0` it is not; a “poll once and return” call can overshoot a zero wait by the full default ask timeout.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:wait_job

chunk_findings.detail: The test discards the `wait_job` result (`_ = RR.wait_job(...)`), so it only verifies that exactly one roborev call was logged. If `wait_job` regressed to return a failed/non-live verdict after the first list read while still making only that one call, the assertion `len(log.read_text().splitlines()) == 1` would still pass. The test’s stated purpose is to prove the bound elapsed between polls returns live, so it should assert `out.live is True` (and ideally the note) to prevent a false-pass on a wrong verdict.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_wait.py:test_a_bound_elapsed_between_polls_returns_live_without_another_read

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier finding still holds: this test only asserts that one log line exists, not that the line is a `list` read. If zero-bound `wait_job` regressed to make a single non-list roborev call (for example `roborev show --job 7`) and returned `live=True, review=None, note="still queued"`, the fake log would still contain one line and the test would pass. The author’s probe about capping the list-read timeout does not make the test assert the logged command is `list`, so the test still does not pin the status read it is named for.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_roborev_wait.py:test_zero_bound_reads_the_status_once_and_reports_it_live

chunk_findings.detail: `json.loads(p.stdout or "[]")` turns an empty stdout (or `None`) from a zero-exit `roborev list --json` into a successful empty job list. Given a daemon that exits 0 and prints nothing, `_read_list` returns `([], "")`, so `wait_job` sees a clean “no jobs” read and can conclude the waited-for job vanished/ended instead of returning a “could not read” note. This contradicts the previous triage’s fix claim that only real `null` or `[]` should read as an empty success; empty output is neither.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `wait_job` makes the standards-gate agent block and poll roborev status until a bound. Given a queued job such as 2917 and a call like `wait_job(repo, 2917, 600)`, the agent process holds for up to 600 seconds and repeatedly invokes `roborev list --json` instead of yielding; that is the agent-side poll-wait/hold that [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] says must not happen. ddflow should express the pending review as a dependency/needs edge or return a pending result for the scheduler to resume, rather than wrapping a blocking wait.

chunk_findings.detail: The fake clock’s sleep stub ignores the requested duration (`lambda s: None`), and the bound-elapsed test’s replacement `leap_past_deadline` also ignores it by advancing the fake clock by 100 regardless of `s`. That means the timeout tests can pass even if `wait_job` asks for an invalid or unbounded sleep. For example, in `test_a_bound_elapsed_between_polls_returns_live_without_another_read`, if `wait_job(repo, 7, 5)` does one `list --json` read and then calls `RR.sleep(100)` (or `RR.sleep(-1)`), the fake clock jumps past the deadline, the function returns the live verdict, and the assertions (`len(calls) == 1`, `out.live is True`, `"still queued" in out.note`) still pass. In production the real sleep would block for 100 seconds past the 5-second bound, or raise on a negative value. The test should record the sleep argument(s) and assert they are nonnegative and within the remaining bound.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing these hooks to `pass_filenames: true` makes ruff receive explicit file paths instead of `.`. Ruff does not apply its `exclude`/`extend-exclude` patterns to explicitly passed paths unless `--force-exclude` is supplied. The new entries (`uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check`) omit that flag. Thus, if the repository’s ruff configuration excludes a tracked Python path (e.g. `[tool.ruff] exclude = ["ddflow/_vendor"]`) and a branch modifies a file under that path, pre-commit will pass it explicitly to ruff and ruff will lint/format-check it, potentially failing the push even though the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` invocation would have skipped the excluded file.

chunk_findings.detail: The new scoping drops the environment’s `SKIP` whenever the command already carries its own leading `SKIP=` assignment. The removed implementation explicitly merged the inherited `SKIP` with the command’s own skip (`SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}..."`), because a shell command-prefix assignment overrides the inherited environment. Now, given environment `SKIP=slow-tests` and `command="SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files"` with a valid `since`, `scope_to_diff` returns `SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD`. When run through the shell, `SKIP` is exactly `lint`, so the `slow-tests` hook is not skipped even though the selected-tests plan set it; the old behavior would have skipped both `slow-tests` and `lint`. This can cause CI to run hooks that were meant to be skipped (or fail because a skipped hook now runs).

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s pre-commit hook will not run in the pre-push stage, so the second test fails (and the first passes vacuously). In `pre-commit`, a hook’s `stages` defaults to `[commit]` unless specified, while `CI.run`’s default command is the pre-push command `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push`. In `test_the_branchs_own_bad_python_still_fails_the_push`, the branch diff contains `mine.py` with `BAD = 2`, but the hook `changed-python-clean` is not selected for the `pre-push` stage, so pre-commit exits successfully without executing the script; `res.status` is `"passed"`, causing the assertion expecting `"failed"` to fail. If `pre-commit` is not installed, the whole file skips, so the intended regression gate may also be silently skipped.

The same applies to other shell metacharacters such as backticks or `$HOME`, changing the command's semantics and potentially executing arbitrary code from a CI command/config value.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing these hooks to `pass_filenames: true` makes ruff receive explicit file paths instead of `.`. Ruff does not apply its `exclude`/`extend-exclude` patterns to explicitly passed paths unless `--force-exclude` is supplied. The new entries (`uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check`) omit that flag. Thus, if the repository’s ruff configuration excludes a tracked Python path (e.g. `[tool.ruff] exclude = ["ddflow/_vendor"]`) and a branch modifies a file under that path, pre-commit will pass it explicitly to ruff and ruff will lint/format-check it, potentially failing the push even though the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` invocation would have skipped the excluded file.
chunk_findings.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml:ruff-check

chunk_findings.detail: The new scoping drops the environment’s `SKIP` whenever the command already carries its own leading `SKIP=` assignment. The removed implementation explicitly merged the inherited `SKIP` with the command’s own skip (`SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}..."`), because a shell command-prefix assignment overrides the inherited environment. Now, given environment `SKIP=slow-tests` and `command="SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files"` with a valid `since`, `scope_to_diff` returns `SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD`. When run through the shell, `SKIP` is exactly `lint`, so the `slow-tests` hook is not skipped even though the selected-tests plan set it; the old behavior would have skipped both `slow-tests` and `lint`. This can cause CI to run hooks that were meant to be skipped (or fail because a skipped hook now runs).
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff`

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s pre-commit hook will not run in the pre-push stage, so the second test fails (and the first passes vacuously). In `pre-commit`, a hook’s `stages` defaults to `[commit]` unless specified, while `CI.run`’s default command is the pre-push command `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push`. In `test_the_branchs_own_bad_python_still_fails_the_push`, the branch diff contains `mine.py` with `BAD = 2`, but the hook `changed-python-clean` is not selected for the `pre-push` stage, so pre-commit exits successfully without executing the script; `res.status` is `"passed"`, causing the assertion expecting `"failed"` to fail. If `pre-commit` is not installed, the whole file skips, so the intended regression gate may also be silently skipped.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert " --to-ref HEAD" in cmd` is an unanchored substring check, so it also matches `--to-ref HEAD~1` (or `--to-ref HEAD^`). If `scope_to_diff` returned `SKIP=frozen-workflow-files pre-commit run --from-ref base --to-ref HEAD~1`, the test would pass even though the CI diff excludes the pushed `HEAD` commit and could miss errors in the tip. The test should require the target ref to be exactly `HEAD`, not merely start with that text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_tripwire_hooks.py:test_the_commands_own_skip_applies_to_the_diff_scoped_run_too

chunk_findings.detail: The new leading-`SKIP=` parser assumes the assignment value is a single non-whitespace token optionally wrapped in one quote layer. A valid shell command such as `SKIP='lint, slow' pre-commit run --all-files` with a valid `since` matches only `SKIP='lint,` because `\S+` stops at the space; `lead.end()` then leaves `slow'` in `run`. The returned command becomes `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint," slow' pre-commit run --from-ref <commit> --to-ref HEAD`, which the shell parses as an unmatched quoted word (`slow'`) instead of invoking `pre-commit`, so the CI command is corrupted rather than preserving the original quoted `SKIP`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `asks_of` unconditionally does `return st.asks`, but a dataclass field default is only applied when `State.__init__` runs. A `State` instance restored without `__init__`—notably a `State` pickled before this change, which the added comment explicitly cites as a supported user—has no `asks` entry in its instance state. Loading such a pickle and calling `asks_of(st)` raises `AttributeError: 'State' object has no attribute 'asks'`, whereas the old `st.__dict__.setdefault("asks", {})` returned an empty dict. Any path that unpickles, `copy.copy`s, or otherwise creates a pre-change `State` without running the generated `__init__` will therefore fail on the first ask read.

chunk_findings.detail: The new unconfirmed exclusion only removes `b.fix_task` from the initial set of non-feature items. If an unconfirmed bug’s `item` is itself a non-feature item, it remains in the returned ids. For example, if `state.items` contains an item `B123` with `branch_kind(B123, cfg) != FEATURE`, and `state.bugs` contains an open bug with `item="B123"`, `fix_task=""`, and `reproduced="no"`, the initial `ids` already contains `B123`; `unconfirmed` contains only the empty fix task, so `difference_update` does not remove `B123`, and the later loop skips the bug because `reproduced == "no"`. The function still returns `B123`, so the unconfirmed bug is still counted/offered, contrary to the stated intent that an unconfirmed bug counts for nothing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/schedule.py:720

chunk_findings.detail: When capture is off, `attach` still executes the repro command before it can know that no bundle will be stored. It calls `RC.check(...)` whenever `repro_cmd` is non-empty, then calls `build(...)`, which returns `None` for capture-off mode, and finally returns `{}`. For example, with `given={"repro_cmd": "touch /tmp/ddflow-marker", "capture": "off"}`, the command is run and the marker is created, but the function records nothing. This makes an “off” capture setting still run arbitrary repro commands and discard their verdict, causing side effects and wasted work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:attach

chunk_findings.detail: The repro command is executed as an argv list, not as a shell command, so common `--repro-cmd` strings are mishandled. Given `cmd="DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE=ci pytest tests/test_x.py"` (the exact environment variable called out in the intent), `shlex.split` produces `["DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE=ci", "pytest", ...]`, and `P.capture(words, ...)` tries to exec the literal program named `DDFLOW_RUNNING_GATE=ci`. No run reaches an exit code, so `_run_at` returns `{"unavailable": "no run reached an exit code to read"}` and the bug is recorded as unconfirmed even though the command would reproduce with that variable set. The same failure applies to `VAR=val cmd`, `&&`, redirections, and shell globs such as `pytest tests/test_*.py`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:check / _run_at

chunk_findings.detail: `tail_bytes` is applied as a character count, not a byte count. With `repro_tail_bytes=1` and a repro command that prints a non-ASCII character such as `é`, `text[-keep:]` stores `"é"`, which is two UTF-8 bytes, exceeding the configured byte budget. `output_truncated` is also computed from character length, not bytes, so byte-limited storage can overflow or silently store more data than `[bugs] repro_tail_bytes` allows.

chunk_findings.detail: Declaring `asks` with `default_factory` only initializes it when `State.__init__` runs. The change explicitly supports instances restored without `__init__` (pre-field pickles), and the new `asks_of` fixes direct reads, but the stated rebuild/redaction coverage is field-walking. For such an instance, `dataclasses.fields(st)` now includes `asks`, yet `getattr(st, "asks")` returns the class-level `dataclasses.Field` object rather than the default `{}` (or, if the walker uses `st.__dict__`, it misses the key entirely). For example, loading a pre-field pickle and running a generic full-state export/redaction over declared fields will process a `Field` object under `asks`, so the ask rows are not treated like other fields and can fail serialization or bypass redaction. The added test only exercises `State.__new__` plus `asks_of`, not the field-walking path.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` to `pass_filenames: true` makes Ruff receive explicit file paths. Ruff, by default, checks explicitly supplied paths even if they match `exclude`/`extend-exclude` or `.gitignore`; the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` respected the project’s Ruff exclusion configuration. With this change, if the repository has any intentionally excluded Python file (for example generated `*_pb2.py`, vendored code, or migrations containing an unused import), a diff-scoped run or `pre-commit run --all-files` that passes that path to `uv run ruff check` will now report the error and fail the push/CI, whereas it was skipped before. The same applies to `ruff format --check` at `.pre-commit-config.yaml:44`. Add `--force-exclude` to both entries (or otherwise filter excluded paths) to preserve the previous semantics.
chunk_findings.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml:38

chunk_findings.detail: `scope_to_diff` validates `since` with `W.rev(tree, since)` but then interpolates the original `since` directly into the shell command string: `command.replace(" --all-files", f" --from-ref {since} --to-ref HEAD", 1)`. If `since` is a ref name containing shell metacharacters (for example a Git ref such as `foo$(touch /tmp/pwn)` or `foo;touch /tmp/pwn`, which can be valid ref names), `W.rev` can resolve it, so the function returns a command like `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref foo$(touch /tmp/pwn) --to-ref HEAD`. When the CI runner executes that command through a shell (as the surrounding command forms, including `SKIP=` prefixes and the previous `rc=0; ...; exit $rc` pattern, require), the shell expands/executes the injected content on the CI machine. The safe value is the commit hash returned by `W.rev`, or the ref must be quoted with `shlex.quote` before interpolation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail:
The test’s lint hook swallows non-“BAD found” grep failures. `SCRIPT` is `#!/bin/sh
if grep -q BAD "$@"; then exit 1; fi
exit 0
`, so it only exits 1 when `grep` exits 0 (marker found). If `grep` exits 2 because a passed file is missing/unreadable, or exits 127 because `grep` is not available, or misparses a filename beginning with `-` as an option, the `if` condition is false and the script falls through to `exit 0`. For example, `scripts/lint.sh deleted.py` returns 0 even though it could not check the file; a diff-scoped pre-commit run that passes a deleted or oddly named file could therefore see the hook “pass” when it did not actually lint the input.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py:SCRIPT

chunk_findings.detail: The new SKIP-merging path rebuilds the leading assignment by inserting the raw captured `SKIP` value inside double quotes, so shell quoting in the original value is not preserved. Given `command = "SKIP='lint' pre-commit run --all-files"` and a resolvable `since`, `_LEADING_SKIP` captures `'lint'` and the function returns `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint'" pre-commit run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`. When this is run through the shell, `SKIP` becomes the literal `'lint'` (or `inherited,'lint'` if `SKIP` was set), not `lint`; pre-commit therefore does not skip the `lint` hook, whereas the previous command preserved `SKIP='lint'` and did skip it. This can cause a hook the command intended to skip to run, potentially failing CI, whenever a leading `SKIP=` assignment uses single quotes or otherwise depends on shell quoting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The new quote-stripping step only checks that the captured `SKIP` token starts and ends with the same quote character; it does not check that those quotes form a single balanced layer around the whole value. For the valid shell command `SKIP='lint','format' pre-commit run --all-files`, the captured raw token is `'lint','format'`. The code strips the first and last single quotes, producing `lint','format`, and rebuilds the command as `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}lint','format" pre-commit run ...`. When executed by a shell, pre-commit receives a `SKIP` value such as `lint','format` (or `inherited,lint','format`), which splits into hook IDs `lint'` and `'format`, not `lint` and `format`, so the intended hooks are not skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: After stripping a quote layer, the value is re-embedded inside double quotes, so characters that were literal inside single quotes become shell-active. Given `SKIP='$(touch /tmp/pwn)' pre-commit run --all-files`, the function returns `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}$(touch /tmp/pwn)" pre-commit run ...`. Executing that with a shell performs command substitution and creates `/tmp/pwn`, whereas the original single-quoted assignment would set `SKIP` to the literal string `$(touch /tmp/pwn)`. The same applies to other shell metacharacters such as backticks or `$HOME`, changing the command's semantics and potentially executing arbitrary code from a CI command/config value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: `_leading_skip` only treats quote characters as grouping, so it does not recognize an unquoted command substitution as part of the leading shell word. For the valid POSIX command `SKIP=$(echo lint) pre-commit run --all-files`, the loop breaks at the space between `echo` and `lint`, returning `own="$(echo"` and `run=" lint) pre-commit run --all-files"`. `scope_to_diff` then emits `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'$(echo' lint) pre-commit run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`; when executed, the stray unquoted `)` is a shell syntax error (and, more generally, the assignment word has been cut in the wrong place). The parser should either handle command substitutions or return `None` for a word it cannot parse instead of producing a malformed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: For the supported case of a `State` restored without `__init__` (`State.__new__(State)` or an old pickle whose `__dict__` lacks `asks`), `State.asks` is a class-level `dataclasses.Field` object because it is declared with `field(default_factory=dict)` in `records.py`. In `asks_of`, `getattr(st, "asks", {})` therefore does not fall back to `{}`; it returns that `Field` object, and `st.__dict__.setdefault("asks", ...)` stores and returns the `Field` object. The added test `test_asks_of_still_lazily_creates_on_a_state_built_without_init` fails at `rows == {}`, and any handler doing `asks_of(st)[ask.id] = row` raises `TypeError: 'Field' object does not support item assignment`. The same object is what field-walking rebuild/redaction sees via `getattr` (or it misses the key if it uses `st.__dict__` before `asks_of`), so the claimed rebuild/redaction coverage is not achieved; the old `setdefault("asks", {})` was the lazy dict creation that worked.

chunk_findings.detail: Declaring `asks` as a dataclass field with `default_factory=dict` makes it part of the generated field set, but an instance restored without `__init__` (the pre-field pickle the docstring explicitly says must still work) has no `asks` in its `__dict__`, and `default_factory` leaves no class-level default. `asks_of` materializes the dict only when called. If a rebuild/redaction/export path, or any normal dataclass field-walker such as `dataclasses.asdict`, `dataclasses.replace`, or the generated `__repr__`/`__eq__`, touches `State` before `asks_of`, it performs `getattr(state, "asks")` and raises `AttributeError: 'State' object has no attribute 'asks'`. For example, loading an old pickle that never had an ask and then walking `dataclasses.fields` to redact or export the full state fails instead of seeing an empty dict. The old side storage was not a declared field, so those helpers did not access it; the change therefore does not provide the promised rebuild/redaction coverage for pre-field instances.

data.reason: 1 finding(s)

chunk_findings.detail: Changing these hooks to `pass_filenames: true` makes ruff receive explicit file paths instead of `.`. Ruff does not apply its `exclude`/`extend-exclude` patterns to explicitly passed paths unless `--force-exclude` is supplied. The new entries (`uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check`) omit that flag. Thus, if the repository’s ruff configuration excludes a tracked Python path (e.g. `[tool.ruff] exclude = ["ddflow/_vendor"]`) and a branch modifies a file under that path, pre-commit will pass it explicitly to ruff and ruff will lint/format-check it, potentially failing the push even though the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` invocation would have skipped the excluded file.
chunk_findings.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml:ruff-check

chunk_findings.detail: The new scoping drops the environment’s `SKIP` whenever the command already carries its own leading `SKIP=` assignment. The removed implementation explicitly merged the inherited `SKIP` with the command’s own skip (`SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}..."`), because a shell command-prefix assignment overrides the inherited environment. Now, given environment `SKIP=slow-tests` and `command="SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files"` with a valid `since`, `scope_to_diff` returns `SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD`. When run through the shell, `SKIP` is exactly `lint`, so the `slow-tests` hook is not skipped even though the selected-tests plan set it; the old behavior would have skipped both `slow-tests` and `lint`. This can cause CI to run hooks that were meant to be skipped (or fail because a skipped hook now runs).
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff`

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s pre-commit hook will not run in the pre-push stage, so the second test fails (and the first passes vacuously). In `pre-commit`, a hook’s `stages` defaults to `[commit]` unless specified, while `CI.run`’s default command is the pre-push command `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push`. In `test_the_branchs_own_bad_python_still_fails_the_push`, the branch diff contains `mine.py` with `BAD = 2`, but the hook `changed-python-clean` is not selected for the `pre-push` stage, so pre-commit exits successfully without executing the script; `res.status` is `"passed"`, causing the assertion expecting `"failed"` to fail. If `pre-commit` is not installed, the whole file skips, so the intended regression gate may also be silently skipped.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert " --to-ref HEAD" in cmd` is an unanchored substring check, so it also matches `--to-ref HEAD~1` (or `--to-ref HEAD^`). If `scope_to_diff` returned `SKIP=frozen-workflow-files pre-commit run --from-ref base --to-ref HEAD~1`, the test would pass even though the CI diff excludes the pushed `HEAD` commit and could miss errors in the tip. The test should require the target ref to be exactly `HEAD`, not merely start with that text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_tripwire_hooks.py:test_the_commands_own_skip_applies_to_the_diff_scoped_run_too

chunk_findings.detail: The new leading-`SKIP=` parser assumes the assignment value is a single non-whitespace token optionally wrapped in one quote layer. A valid shell command such as `SKIP='lint, slow' pre-commit run --all-files` with a valid `since` matches only `SKIP='lint,` because `\S+` stops at the space; `lead.end()` then leaves `slow'` in `run`. The returned command becomes `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint," slow' pre-commit run --from-ref <commit> --to-ref HEAD`, which the shell parses as an unmatched quoted word (`slow'`) instead of invoking `pre-commit`, so the CI command is corrupted rather than preserving the original quoted `SKIP`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_LEADING_SKIP

chunk_findings.detail: The double-quote branch of `_leading_skip` does not implement shell escaping: inside a double-quoted `SKIP` value it treats a backslash as an ordinary character and the following `"` as a closing quote. For the valid shell command `SKIP="lint\"slow" pre-commit run --all-files` with an inherited environment `SKIP=slow-tests`, the parser closes the quote at `\"`, then treats the real closing quote as opening a new quote and returns `None` because it ends inside a quote. `scope_to_diff` then emits the original assignment unchanged except for the `--all-files` rewrite, e.g. `SKIP="lint\"slow" pre-commit run --from-ref <commit> --to-ref HEAD`. The shell sets `SKIP` to `lint"slow`, shadowing `slow-tests`, so the inherited skip is not merged and the skipped hook/test runs. The same escaping bug can also split a valid command inside a quoted value (`SKIP="\" --all-files" ...`) and rewrite the `--all-files` that belongs to the `SKIP` value, producing a malformed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test only checks prefixes for the `lint, slow` and empty-`SKIP` cases, and only checks the scoped suffix for the `$(echo pwn)` case; it never asserts that `--all-files` has been removed for any of the new inputs. Thus a `scope_to_diff` implementation that returned, for example, `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'lint, slow' pre-commit run --all-files` or `SKIP="" pre-commit run --all-files` would satisfy the assertions even though the command would still lint the whole tree, which is the behavior the change is supposed to prevent. It should assert `--all-files` absence and the exact `--from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD` suffix for all three quoted/empty-`SKIP` cases.

chunk_findings.detail: When `--gate` is omitted, the printed “recipe” hard-codes `--gate G` instead of using the gate that `RS.show` actually resolved and reports in `out.data["gate"]`. For example, if `ddflow review triage ITEM` is run with no `--gate` and the recorded round being listed is under the `critic` gate, `RS.show` returns `data["gate"] == "critic"`, so the structured payload says `gate: critic`, but the human text tells the user to run `ddflow review triage ITEM --gate G --finding N ...`. Following the recipe records the verdict under the wrong/nonexistent gate or fails, while the code already had the correct gate available.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` to `pass_filenames: true` makes Ruff receive explicit file paths. Ruff, by default, checks explicitly supplied paths even if they match `exclude`/`extend-exclude` or `.gitignore`; the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` respected the project’s Ruff exclusion configuration. With this change, if the repository has any intentionally excluded Python file (for example generated `*_pb2.py`, vendored code, or migrations containing an unused import), a diff-scoped run or `pre-commit run --all-files` that passes that path to `uv run ruff check` will now report the error and fail the push/CI, whereas it was skipped before. The same applies to `ruff format --check` at `.pre-commit-config.yaml:44`. Add `--force-exclude` to both entries (or otherwise filter excluded paths) to preserve the previous semantics.
chunk_findings.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml:38

chunk_findings.detail: `scope_to_diff` validates `since` with `W.rev(tree, since)` but then interpolates the original `since` directly into the shell command string: `command.replace(" --all-files", f" --from-ref {since} --to-ref HEAD", 1)`. If `since` is a ref name containing shell metacharacters (for example a Git ref such as `foo$(touch /tmp/pwn)` or `foo;touch /tmp/pwn`, which can be valid ref names), `W.rev` can resolve it, so the function returns a command like `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref foo$(touch /tmp/pwn) --to-ref HEAD`. When the CI runner executes that command through a shell (as the surrounding command forms, including `SKIP=` prefixes and the previous `rc=0; ...; exit $rc` pattern, require), the shell expands/executes the injected content on the CI machine. The safe value is the commit hash returned by `W.rev`, or the ref must be quoted with `shlex.quote` before interpolation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail:
The test’s lint hook swallows non-“BAD found” grep failures. `SCRIPT` is `#!/bin/sh
if grep -q BAD "$@"; then exit 1; fi
exit 0
`, so it only exits 1 when `grep` exits 0 (marker found). If `grep` exits 2 because a passed file is missing/unreadable, or exits 127 because `grep` is not available, or misparses a filename beginning with `-` as an option, the `if` condition is false and the script falls through to `exit 0`. For example, `scripts/lint.sh deleted.py` returns 0 even though it could not check the file; a diff-scoped pre-commit run that passes a deleted or oddly named file could therefore see the hook “pass” when it did not actually lint the input.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py:SCRIPT

chunk_findings.detail: The new SKIP-merging path rebuilds the leading assignment by inserting the raw captured `SKIP` value inside double quotes, so shell quoting in the original value is not preserved. Given `command = "SKIP='lint' pre-commit run --all-files"` and a resolvable `since`, `_LEADING_SKIP` captures `'lint'` and the function returns `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint'" pre-commit run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`. When this is run through the shell, `SKIP` becomes the literal `'lint'` (or `inherited,'lint'` if `SKIP` was set), not `lint`; pre-commit therefore does not skip the `lint` hook, whereas the previous command preserved `SKIP='lint'` and did skip it. This can cause a hook the command intended to skip to run, potentially failing CI, whenever a leading `SKIP=` assignment uses single quotes or otherwise depends on shell quoting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The new quote-stripping step only checks that the captured `SKIP` token starts and ends with the same quote character; it does not check that those quotes form a single balanced layer around the whole value. For the valid shell command `SKIP='lint','format' pre-commit run --all-files`, the captured raw token is `'lint','format'`. The code strips the first and last single quotes, producing `lint','format`, and rebuilds the command as `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}lint','format" pre-commit run ...`. When executed by a shell, pre-commit receives a `SKIP` value such as `lint','format` (or `inherited,lint','format`), which splits into hook IDs `lint'` and `'format`, not `lint` and `format`, so the intended hooks are not skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: After stripping a quote layer, the value is re-embedded inside double quotes, so characters that were literal inside single quotes become shell-active. Given `SKIP='$(touch /tmp/pwn)' pre-commit run --all-files`, the function returns `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}$(touch /tmp/pwn)" pre-commit run ...`. Executing that with a shell performs command substitution and creates `/tmp/pwn`, whereas the original single-quoted assignment would set `SKIP` to the literal string `$(touch /tmp/pwn)`. The same applies to other shell metacharacters such as backticks or `$HOME`, changing the command's semantics and potentially executing arbitrary code from a CI command/config value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: `_leading_skip` only treats quote characters as grouping, so it does not recognize an unquoted command substitution as part of the leading shell word. For the valid POSIX command `SKIP=$(echo lint) pre-commit run --all-files`, the loop breaks at the space between `echo` and `lint`, returning `own="$(echo"` and `run=" lint) pre-commit run --all-files"`. `scope_to_diff` then emits `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'$(echo' lint) pre-commit run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`; when executed, the stray unquoted `)` is a shell syntax error (and, more generally, the assignment word has been cut in the wrong place). The parser should either handle command substitutions or return `None` for a word it cannot parse instead of producing a malformed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The parser treats only whitespace as terminating the leading `SKIP=` word, not shell operators. Given the shell command `SKIP=lint;pre-commit run --all-files`, the shell parses the assignment value as `lint` and the remainder as `;pre-commit run --all-files`, but `_leading_skip` consumes the `;` and the following `pre-commit` until the next space, returning own `lint;pre-commit` and rest ` run --all-files`. `scope_to_diff` then rebuilds something like `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint;pre-commit' run --all-files`, so the actual `pre-commit` command is swallowed into the SKIP value and the command tries to run `run`. Even `SKIP=lint; pre-commit run --all-files` keeps the `;` in the literal SKIP and skips the intended merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The double-quoted branch does not implement shell backslash escapes. For a valid command whose characters after `SKIP=` are double quote, backslash, backslash, double quote (`SKIP="\\"` in shell source), the shell resolves the assignment value to one backslash, but the code appends both backslashes and returns own `\\`; `scope_to_diff` then re-emits the wrong literal. The same branch also treats an escaped closing double quote as closing the quote, so an unbalanced shell word such as double quote, `a`, backslash, double quote, space is accepted as own `a\` instead of returning `None` as the docstring requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: When `_leading_skip` returns `None`, the original leading assignment is left in the command and the existing diff-scoping step replaces the first ` --all-files` in the whole string. Given `SKIP=$(echo --all-files) pre-commit run --all-files`, the first ` --all-files` is the argument to `echo`, not the pre-commit flag, so the returned command becomes `SKIP=$(echo --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD) pre-commit run --all-files`: the pre-commit run is not scoped and the command substitution is corrupted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The change introduces a blocking poll loop (`_POLL_S = 5.0`, module-level `sleep`, and the new `wait_job` helper) and documents it as the command agents should run (`python -m ddflow.services.roborev wait --job N`). That is a poll-wait/hold: e.g. running the new command with a 600-second timeout will call `roborev list --json`, sleep for five seconds, and repeat for up to ten minutes while the agent is blocked, rather than expressing the dependency through ddflow’s needs-edge/self-healing mechanism. This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], whose advisory rule says agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/roborev.py:_POLL_S / wait_job

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds a `wait_job` helper that polls `roborev` status and (per the intent) waits with lease renewal. This is exactly the poll-wait/hold pattern prohibited by [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]: agents should not poll-wait or hold while waiting; ddflow should self-heal waits via needs edges or record unavailability without holding. Concretely, when the standards gate invokes this helper while job 2917 is still queued, the agent will sleep/poll for the configured bound and hold its lease instead of being unblocked by the self-healing mechanism.

chunk_findings.detail: The argparse setup adds a positional `wait` with `nargs="?"` but never checks that the supplied token is actually `wait` (or omitted). Given `python -m ddflow.services.roborev show --job 1`, argparse accepts `show` as the positional, parses `--job`, and then `main` calls `wait_job(...)` anyway. If job 1 is still queued, this silently performs a bounded wait and may block/print progress instead of rejecting the unsupported subcommand or showing the job.

chunk_findings.detail: The live note recommends `python -m ddflow.services.roborev wait --job {job}` as “the one sure way forward,” but it omits the repository argument. If the original command was run as `python -m ddflow.services.roborev wait --job N --repo /path/to/repo`, following the printed advice runs in the current directory; when that directory is not the repository holding the job, the follow-up command will report that roborev holds no such job and exit 2, even though the original wait was correctly scoped.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `wait_job` implements a polling wait loop: it repeatedly reads `roborev list`, prints progress, and calls `sleep(min(_POLL_S, left))` while holding the caller. The recorded advisory rule [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] states that agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting and that ddflow should unblock via dependency edges rather than waiting loops. This change directly introduces such a poll-wait/hold, violating that guidance item.
chunk_findings.title: [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] ddflow/services/roborev.py:wait_job

chunk_findings.detail: This test (and the `wait_job` helper it exercises) encodes a sleep/poll wait loop: it calls `RR.wait_job(repo, 7, 3)` with a fake clock/sleep and asserts the helper polled through the bound (`reads >= 2`) and slept between polls. That is the poll-waiting pattern the advisory rule says should not be used; the rule says agents should not poll-wait or hold while waiting and ddflow should heal blockage by adding needs edges. For the standards gate, this should be modeled as a dependency/blockage edge rather than a bounded sleep-poll helper. [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]

chunk_findings.detail: The JSON value produced by `_add_globs_arg` is still interpolated into the advice inside literal single quotes. `json.dumps` does not escape a single quote/apostrophe, so a staged path containing one produces an advice command that is not shell-safe. For example, if an uncovered path is `src/a'b.py`, the hook prints `ddflow update <ID> --add-globs '["src/a'b.py"]'`; in a POSIX shell the apostrophe terminates the single-quoted argument and the following JSON double quote can make the command syntactically invalid or cause it to add a different glob (e.g. `src/ab.py`) rather than the literal path `src/a'b.py`. The docstring’s claim that the JSON form is “safe between single quotes” is therefore wrong; the value needs shell quoting such as `shlex.quote(json.dumps(...))`.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing these hooks to `pass_filenames: true` makes ruff receive explicit file paths instead of `.`. Ruff does not apply its `exclude`/`extend-exclude` patterns to explicitly passed paths unless `--force-exclude` is supplied. The new entries (`uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check`) omit that flag. Thus, if the repository’s ruff configuration excludes a tracked Python path (e.g. `[tool.ruff] exclude = ["ddflow/_vendor"]`) and a branch modifies a file under that path, pre-commit will pass it explicitly to ruff and ruff will lint/format-check it, potentially failing the push even though the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` invocation would have skipped the excluded file.
chunk_findings.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml:ruff-check

chunk_findings.detail: The new scoping drops the environment’s `SKIP` whenever the command already carries its own leading `SKIP=` assignment. The removed implementation explicitly merged the inherited `SKIP` with the command’s own skip (`SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}..."`), because a shell command-prefix assignment overrides the inherited environment. Now, given environment `SKIP=slow-tests` and `command="SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files"` with a valid `since`, `scope_to_diff` returns `SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD`. When run through the shell, `SKIP` is exactly `lint`, so the `slow-tests` hook is not skipped even though the selected-tests plan set it; the old behavior would have skipped both `slow-tests` and `lint`. This can cause CI to run hooks that were meant to be skipped (or fail because a skipped hook now runs).
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff`

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s pre-commit hook will not run in the pre-push stage, so the second test fails (and the first passes vacuously). In `pre-commit`, a hook’s `stages` defaults to `[commit]` unless specified, while `CI.run`’s default command is the pre-push command `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push`. In `test_the_branchs_own_bad_python_still_fails_the_push`, the branch diff contains `mine.py` with `BAD = 2`, but the hook `changed-python-clean` is not selected for the `pre-push` stage, so pre-commit exits successfully without executing the script; `res.status` is `"passed"`, causing the assertion expecting `"failed"` to fail. If `pre-commit` is not installed, the whole file skips, so the intended regression gate may also be silently skipped.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py:31

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert " --to-ref HEAD" in cmd` is an unanchored substring check, so it also matches `--to-ref HEAD~1` (or `--to-ref HEAD^`). If `scope_to_diff` returned `SKIP=frozen-workflow-files pre-commit run --from-ref base --to-ref HEAD~1`, the test would pass even though the CI diff excludes the pushed `HEAD` commit and could miss errors in the tip. The test should require the target ref to be exactly `HEAD`, not merely start with that text.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_tripwire_hooks.py:test_the_commands_own_skip_applies_to_the_diff_scoped_run_too

chunk_findings.detail: The new leading-`SKIP=` parser assumes the assignment value is a single non-whitespace token optionally wrapped in one quote layer. A valid shell command such as `SKIP='lint, slow' pre-commit run --all-files` with a valid `since` matches only `SKIP='lint,` because `\S+` stops at the space; `lead.end()` then leaves `slow'` in `run`. The returned command becomes `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint," slow' pre-commit run --from-ref <commit> --to-ref HEAD`, which the shell parses as an unmatched quoted word (`slow'`) instead of invoking `pre-commit`, so the CI command is corrupted rather than preserving the original quoted `SKIP`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_LEADING_SKIP

chunk_findings.detail: The double-quote branch of `_leading_skip` does not implement shell escaping: inside a double-quoted `SKIP` value it treats a backslash as an ordinary character and the following `"` as a closing quote. For the valid shell command `SKIP="lint\"slow" pre-commit run --all-files` with an inherited environment `SKIP=slow-tests`, the parser closes the quote at `\"`, then treats the real closing quote as opening a new quote and returns `None` because it ends inside a quote. `scope_to_diff` then emits the original assignment unchanged except for the `--all-files` rewrite, e.g. `SKIP="lint\"slow" pre-commit run --from-ref <commit> --to-ref HEAD`. The shell sets `SKIP` to `lint"slow`, shadowing `slow-tests`, so the inherited skip is not merged and the skipped hook/test runs. The same escaping bug can also split a valid command inside a quoted value (`SKIP="\" --all-files" ...`) and rewrite the `--all-files` that belongs to the `SKIP` value, producing a malformed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test only checks prefixes for the `lint, slow` and empty-`SKIP` cases, and only checks the scoped suffix for the `$(echo pwn)` case; it never asserts that `--all-files` has been removed for any of the new inputs. Thus a `scope_to_diff` implementation that returned, for example, `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'lint, slow' pre-commit run --all-files` or `SKIP="" pre-commit run --all-files` would satisfy the assertions even though the command would still lint the whole tree, which is the behavior the change is supposed to prevent. It should assert `--all-files` absence and the exact `--from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD` suffix for all three quoted/empty-`SKIP` cases.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_tripwire_hooks.py:test_quoted_skip_values_stay_literal_and_an_empty_one_stays_an_override

chunk_findings.detail: The new double-quote scanner still does not implement shell backslash escapes. Inside `"..."` it appends a backslash as an ordinary character and then processes the following character as if it were unescaped. For the valid command text `SKIP="a\\b" pre-commit run --all-files` (two backslash characters between the quotes), the shell would resolve the assignment value to `a\b`, but `_leading_skip` returns `a\\b` with `active=False`, so the surrounding `scope_to_diff` path rebuilds a single-quoted literal containing two backslashes and the CI run receives a different SKIP value. The same branch also treats `SKIP="lint\$slow" ...` as active even though `\$` is a literal `$`, causing the inherited SKIP not to be merged. This contradicts the docstring’s “value the shell would resolve it to” and the earlier requirement to merge a parseable leading SKIP with the environment’s SKIP.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The new advice puts staged paths directly into a `--add-globs` value without escaping glob metacharacters. For a staged path such as `src/[abc].py`, `_add_globs_arg(['src/[abc].py'])` returns `'["src/[abc].py"]'`, so the hook prints `ddflow update <ID> --add-globs '["src/[abc].py"]'`. The option takes globs, and standard glob/fnmatch semantics treat `[abc]` as a character class, so that added glob matches `src/a.py`, `src/b.py`, or `src/c.py` but not the literal staged path `src/[abc].py`; an agent following the advice updates the claim and the commit hook still refuses (and for paths containing `*` or `?`, the advice over-covers unrelated files). The JSON quoting fixes comma splitting but not glob escaping.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_add_globs_arg

chunk_findings.detail: The new advice puts staged paths verbatim into the glob list, without escaping glob metacharacters. The test `test_the_refusal_advice_keeps_a_comma_path_whole` enforces exactly this shape: the path string is JSON-encoded and shell-quoted, but not glob-escaped. Given a staged path containing a glob metacharacter, e.g. `src/a[1].py` (valid on POSIX), the hook will print something like `ddflow update <ID> --add-globs '["src/a[1].py"]'`. Since `--add-globs` takes globs, `src/a[1].py` is a character-class pattern matching `src/a1.py`, not the literal staged file; after following the advice the lease still does not cover `src/a[1].py`, so the commit remains refused. For a path like `src/a*.py`, the same advice would instead add a wildcard covering many files, widening the lease unintentionally.

chunk_findings.detail: When `--gate` is omitted, the printed “recipe” hard-codes `--gate G` instead of using the gate that `RS.show` actually resolved and reports in `out.data["gate"]`. For example, if `ddflow review triage ITEM` is run with no `--gate` and the recorded round being listed is under the `critic` gate, `RS.show` returns `data["gate"] == "critic"`, so the structured payload says `gate: critic`, but the human text tells the user to run `ddflow review triage ITEM --gate G --finding N ...`. Following the recipe records the verdict under the wrong/nonexistent gate or fails, while the code already had the correct gate available.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/review.py:_list_verb

chunk_findings.detail: The new CLI regression test only exercises `review triage T1 --gate critic` as a listing. It never exercises the grammar symptom named in the bug: `review <id> --finding N --refuted` (bare or under the new verb). A change that makes the no-flag listing work but still leaves argparse rejecting `--finding/--refuted`, or that only fixes the API path while the CLI still errors, would pass this test. Given the stated regression input `review <id> --finding 1 --refuted`, the test suite does not guard that path.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_triage_missing_the_verdict_still_prints_the_findings_first` checks only the exit code and the order of words in `out.reason`. It does not check that the missing-verdict `api.triage` call records no live round or no triage event. If `api.triage(repo, "T1", gate="critic", finding=1, verdict="")` still enqueues a review round while returning a reason whose text happens to mention findings before “say which”, the test passes despite the core “reading/listing must not spend a round” promise being broken.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_listing_no_round.py:50-57

chunk_findings.detail: The new recipe construction discards all but the first gate whenever the listing result reports more than one gate. The added comment says `out.data["gate"]` can be a comma-separated list of gates, and the code takes `read_gate.split(",")[0]`. If a listing reads two gates, for example `ddflow review triage T1 --gate critic,security` (or an omitted `--gate` where `RS.show` returns `"critic,security"`), the printed recipe becomes `ddflow review triage T1 --gate critic --finding N ...`. If the user copies that recipe for a finding that belongs to `security`, the verdict is recorded against `critic` or the CLI errors because that finding does not exist under `critic`; the previous behavior preserved the full gate value.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing `ruff-check` and `ruff-format` to `pass_filenames: true` makes Ruff receive explicit file paths. Ruff, by default, checks explicitly supplied paths even if they match `exclude`/`extend-exclude` or `.gitignore`; the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` respected the project’s Ruff exclusion configuration. With this change, if the repository has any intentionally excluded Python file (for example generated `*_pb2.py`, vendored code, or migrations containing an unused import), a diff-scoped run or `pre-commit run --all-files` that passes that path to `uv run ruff check` will now report the error and fail the push/CI, whereas it was skipped before. The same applies to `ruff format --check` at `.pre-commit-config.yaml:44`. Add `--force-exclude` to both entries (or otherwise filter excluded paths) to preserve the previous semantics.
chunk_findings.title: .pre-commit-config.yaml:38

chunk_findings.detail: `scope_to_diff` validates `since` with `W.rev(tree, since)` but then interpolates the original `since` directly into the shell command string: `command.replace(" --all-files", f" --from-ref {since} --to-ref HEAD", 1)`. If `since` is a ref name containing shell metacharacters (for example a Git ref such as `foo$(touch /tmp/pwn)` or `foo;touch /tmp/pwn`, which can be valid ref names), `W.rev` can resolve it, so the function returns a command like `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref foo$(touch /tmp/pwn) --to-ref HEAD`. When the CI runner executes that command through a shell (as the surrounding command forms, including `SKIP=` prefixes and the previous `rc=0; ...; exit $rc` pattern, require), the shell expands/executes the injected content on the CI machine. The safe value is the commit hash returned by `W.rev`, or the ref must be quoted with `shlex.quote` before interpolation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail:
The test’s lint hook swallows non-“BAD found” grep failures. `SCRIPT` is `#!/bin/sh
if grep -q BAD "$@"; then exit 1; fi
exit 0
`, so it only exits 1 when `grep` exits 0 (marker found). If `grep` exits 2 because a passed file is missing/unreadable, or exits 127 because `grep` is not available, or misparses a filename beginning with `-` as an option, the `if` condition is false and the script falls through to `exit 0`. For example, `scripts/lint.sh deleted.py` returns 0 even though it could not check the file; a diff-scoped pre-commit run that passes a deleted or oddly named file could therefore see the hook “pass” when it did not actually lint the input.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_diff_scope.py:SCRIPT

chunk_findings.detail: The new SKIP-merging path rebuilds the leading assignment by inserting the raw captured `SKIP` value inside double quotes, so shell quoting in the original value is not preserved. Given `command = "SKIP='lint' pre-commit run --all-files"` and a resolvable `since`, `_LEADING_SKIP` captures `'lint'` and the function returns `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint'" pre-commit run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`. When this is run through the shell, `SKIP` becomes the literal `'lint'` (or `inherited,'lint'` if `SKIP` was set), not `lint`; pre-commit therefore does not skip the `lint` hook, whereas the previous command preserved `SKIP='lint'` and did skip it. This can cause a hook the command intended to skip to run, potentially failing CI, whenever a leading `SKIP=` assignment uses single quotes or otherwise depends on shell quoting.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The new quote-stripping step only checks that the captured `SKIP` token starts and ends with the same quote character; it does not check that those quotes form a single balanced layer around the whole value. For the valid shell command `SKIP='lint','format' pre-commit run --all-files`, the captured raw token is `'lint','format'`. The code strips the first and last single quotes, producing `lint','format`, and rebuilds the command as `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}lint','format" pre-commit run ...`. When executed by a shell, pre-commit receives a `SKIP` value such as `lint','format` (or `inherited,lint','format`), which splits into hook IDs `lint'` and `'format`, not `lint` and `format`, so the intended hooks are not skipped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: After stripping a quote layer, the value is re-embedded inside double quotes, so characters that were literal inside single quotes become shell-active. Given `SKIP='$(touch /tmp/pwn)' pre-commit run --all-files`, the function returns `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}$(touch /tmp/pwn)" pre-commit run ...`. Executing that with a shell performs command substitution and creates `/tmp/pwn`, whereas the original single-quoted assignment would set `SKIP` to the literal string `$(touch /tmp/pwn)`. The same applies to other shell metacharacters such as backticks or `$HOME`, changing the command's semantics and potentially executing arbitrary code from a CI command/config value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: `_leading_skip` only treats quote characters as grouping, so it does not recognize an unquoted command substitution as part of the leading shell word. For the valid POSIX command `SKIP=$(echo lint) pre-commit run --all-files`, the loop breaks at the space between `echo` and `lint`, returning `own="$(echo"` and `run=" lint) pre-commit run --all-files"`. `scope_to_diff` then emits `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'$(echo' lint) pre-commit run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`; when executed, the stray unquoted `)` is a shell syntax error (and, more generally, the assignment word has been cut in the wrong place). The parser should either handle command substitutions or return `None` for a word it cannot parse instead of producing a malformed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The parser treats only whitespace as terminating the leading `SKIP=` word, not shell operators. Given the shell command `SKIP=lint;pre-commit run --all-files`, the shell parses the assignment value as `lint` and the remainder as `;pre-commit run --all-files`, but `_leading_skip` consumes the `;` and the following `pre-commit` until the next space, returning own `lint;pre-commit` and rest ` run --all-files`. `scope_to_diff` then rebuilds something like `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}'lint;pre-commit' run --all-files`, so the actual `pre-commit` command is swallowed into the SKIP value and the command tries to run `run`. Even `SKIP=lint; pre-commit run --all-files` keeps the `;` in the literal SKIP and skips the intended merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The double-quoted branch does not implement shell backslash escapes. For a valid command whose characters after `SKIP=` are double quote, backslash, backslash, double quote (`SKIP="\\"` in shell source), the shell resolves the assignment value to one backslash, but the code appends both backslashes and returns own `\\`; `scope_to_diff` then re-emits the wrong literal. The same branch also treats an escaped closing double quote as closing the quote, so an unbalanced shell word such as double quote, `a`, backslash, double quote, space is accepted as own `a\` instead of returning `None` as the docstring requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: When `_leading_skip` returns `None`, the original leading assignment is left in the command and the existing diff-scoping step replaces the first ` --all-files` in the whole string. Given `SKIP=$(echo --all-files) pre-commit run --all-files`, the first ` --all-files` is the argument to `echo`, not the pre-commit flag, so the returned command becomes `SKIP=$(echo --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD) pre-commit run --all-files`: the pre-commit run is not scoped and the command substitution is corrupted.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: The parser still ends the leading `SKIP=` word only on whitespace; it does not stop at shell operators. Given the valid shell command `SKIP=lint;pre-commit run --all-files`, the loop consumes `lint;pre-commit` as the assignment value and leaves ` run --all-files` as the rest. `scope_to_diff` then rebuilds a command like `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'lint;pre-commit' run --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD`, which runs `run` instead of `pre-commit` and sets `SKIP` to a value containing the command name. The new change only adds double-quote escape handling and does not address this operator boundary problem.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The visible parser still marks unquoted `$` as shell-active, so a command such as `SKIP=$(echo --all-files) pre-commit run --all-files` is declined by `_leading_skip` (or at least cannot be safely re-quoted). `scope_to_diff` then performs its global replacement of the first ` --all-files` in the whole command string, which is the argument to `echo`, producing `SKIP=$(echo --from-ref <sha> --to-ref HEAD) pre-commit run --all-files`. That corrupts the command substitution and leaves the actual `pre-commit run` invocation unscoped. The new diff does not make the diff-scoping replacement aware of command-substitution boundaries.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff

chunk_findings.detail: `delta_rounds` does not exclude runs marked `retry_of_partial`, unlike `full_rounds`. Given a gate history containing two delta runs: first with evidence `{review_kind: "delta", status: "PARTIAL"}` and second with evidence `{review_kind: "delta", status: "REVIEWED", retry_of_partial: True}` (a retry of the already-counted partial delta), both satisfy the `delta_rounds` filter, so `delta_rounds` and `rounds_used` return 2. chunk_findings.detail: The new repro-check path is outside the exception guard that is supposed to make evidence collection non-fatal. The lines compute `run` by calling `RC.check(...)` (and `F.tree(repo).get(...)` plus `int(cfg.bugs.repro_runs)` / `float(cfg.bugs.repro_test_timeout_s)` / `int(cfg.bugs.repro_tail_bytes)`) before entering the `try` block, so any exception there propagates out of `attach` instead of returning `{"repro": {"unavailable": ...}}`. For example, if `bug found --repro-cmd 'pytest tests/test_x.py'` is run with a repro knob that cannot be coerced (e.g. `bugs.repro_runs = "5.0"` raises `ValueError` in `int(...)`) or if the scratch-checkout helper in `RC.check` raises because the recorded sha/tree is not available, the `bug found` operation fails rather than filing the bug with unavailable evidence. That violates the function’s own contract: “Filing a bug must never fail for want of evidence.” The repro run should be performed inside the same guarded path (or otherwise caught), with `run = None` on failure, so `attach` can still return an `unavailable` link and the bug is not lost.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprobundle.py:attach (the `RC.check(...)` call before the `try` block)

chunk_findings.detail: `output_truncated` is computed from the already-truncated per-run tails, so it can report “not truncated” even when the command’s output was cut. For example, with `repro_runs=1` and `repro_tail_bytes=1`, a repro command that prints `ab` and exits successfully causes `_run_at` to append only `shot.out[-1:]` (`"b"`). The final `raw` length is 1, so `record["output_truncated"]` is set to `False` and `record["output"]` is `"b"`, even though the first byte was discarded. For the common default of one run, any ASCII output longer than `repro_tail_bytes` will produce `output_truncated: False`, misleading consumers into treating the stored tail as the full repro output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/reprocheck.py:_run_at

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that the repro command is run in a scratch checkout of the recorded sha, but it does not actually pin that behavior. `touch ran.txt` succeeds in any writable directory, and the only “sha” check is `assert run["at"]`, which accepts any truthy value. If the implementation executes the command in a plain temporary directory, or in a copy of the current tree, and merely records the current sha or a timestamp in `at`, the test still passes: `proj/ran.txt` is absent, `executed is True`, `at` is truthy, and `reproduced == "no"`. Thus a wrong implementation that does not run the command at the recorded sha in a scratch checkout would be accepted by this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repro_bundle.py:test_repro_cmd_is_run_at_the_recorded_sha_in_a_scratch_checkout

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to pin that the `repro_tail_bytes` budget bounds memory ("each run's output is pre-cut when it lands"), but it only exercises three runs that emit 11 bytes each and then checks the final 8-byte tail. It therefore passes unchanged even if `_run_at` still accumulates the full stdout of every run before tailing it; the previously confirmed OOM scenario (`repro_runs=10`, `repro_tail_bytes=1024`, a command printing hundreds of megabytes per run) is not exercised. As written, this test does not answer the earlier confirmed memory finding and gives false confidence that the memory bound is pinned.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_repro_verify.py:test_each_runs_output_is_bounded_before_the_tail_is_cut

chunk_findings.detail: The hook advice now prints a JSON array as the value of `--add-globs`, but the same change advertises the `--add-globs` value as comma-separated in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py` (`--add-globs <comma,separated>`), and the diff contains no change making the CLI parser JSON-aware. chunk_findings.detail: The advice inserts literal staged paths directly as glob patterns without escaping glob metacharacters. For a staged path such as `src/a[b].py`, the advice adds the glob `src/a[b].py`; under standard glob semantics `[b]` is a character class, so it matches `src/ab.py` rather than the literal path `src/a[b].py`, leaving the commit still refused. Conversely, a literal path containing `*`, such as `src/*.py`, would be added as a pattern matching all `.py` files, unintentionally widening the lease beyond the staged path.

chunk_findings.detail: Changing these hooks to `pass_filenames: true` makes ruff receive explicit file paths instead of `.`. Ruff does not apply its `exclude`/`extend-exclude` patterns to explicitly passed paths unless `--force-exclude` is supplied. The new entries (`uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check`) omit that flag. Thus, if the repository’s ruff configuration excludes a tracked Python path (e.g. `[tool.ruff] exclude = ["ddflow/_vendor"]`) and a branch modifies a file under that path, pre-commit will pass it explicitly to ruff and ruff will lint/format-check it, potentially failing the push even though the previous `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .` invocation would have skipped the excluded file.

chunk_findings.detail: The new scoping drops the environment’s `SKIP` whenever the command already carries its own leading `SKIP=` assignment. The removed implementation explicitly merged the inherited `SKIP` with the command’s own skip (`SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}..."`), because a shell command-prefix assignment overrides the inherited environment. Now, given environment `SKIP=slow-tests` and `command="SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --all-files"` with a valid `since`, `scope_to_diff` returns `SKIP=lint pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push --from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD`. When run through the shell, `SKIP` is exactly `lint`, so the `slow-tests` hook is not skipped even though the selected-tests plan set it; the old behavior would have skipped both `slow-tests` and `lint`. This can cause CI to run hooks that were meant to be skipped (or fail because a skipped hook now runs).
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/ci.py:scope_to_diff`

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test’s pre-commit hook will not run in the pre-push stage, so the second test fails (and the first passes vacuously). In `pre-commit`, a hook’s `stages` defaults to `[commit]` unless specified, while `CI.run`’s default command is the pre-push command `pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push`. In `test_the_branchs_own_bad_python_still_fails_the_push`, the branch diff contains `mine.py` with `BAD = 2`, but the hook `changed-python-clean` is not selected for the `pre-push` stage, so pre-commit exits successfully without executing the script; `res.status` is `"passed"`, causing the assertion expecting `"failed"` to fail. If `pre-commit` is not installed, the whole file skips, so the intended regression gate may also be silently skipped.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert " --to-ref HEAD" in cmd` is an unanchored substring check, so it also matches `--to-ref HEAD~1` (or `--to-ref HEAD^`). chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_LEADING_SKIP

chunk_findings.detail: The double-quote branch of `_leading_skip` does not implement shell escaping: inside a double-quoted `SKIP` value it treats a backslash as an ordinary character and the following `"` as a closing quote. For the valid shell command `SKIP="lint\"slow" pre-commit run --all-files` with an inherited environment `SKIP=slow-tests`, the parser closes the quote at `\"`, then treats the real closing quote as opening a new quote and returns `None` because it ends inside a quote. `scope_to_diff` then emits the original assignment unchanged except for the `--all-files` rewrite, e.g. `SKIP="lint\"slow" pre-commit run --from-ref <commit> --to-ref HEAD`. The shell sets `SKIP` to `lint"slow`, shadowing `slow-tests`, so the inherited skip is not merged and the skipped hook/test runs. The same escaping bug can also split a valid command inside a quoted value (`SKIP="\" --all-files" ...`) and rewrite the `--all-files` that belongs to the `SKIP` value, producing a malformed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The new regression test only checks prefixes for the `lint, slow` and empty-`SKIP` cases, and only checks the scoped suffix for the `$(echo pwn)` case; it never asserts that `--all-files` has been removed for any of the new inputs. Thus a `scope_to_diff` implementation that returned, for example, `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'lint, slow' pre-commit run --all-files` or `SKIP="" pre-commit run --all-files` would satisfy the assertions even though the command would still lint the whole tree, which is the behavior the change is supposed to prevent. It should assert `--all-files` absence and the exact `--from-ref <since> --to-ref HEAD` suffix for all three quoted/empty-`SKIP` cases.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ci_tripwire_hooks.py:test_quoted_skip_values_stay_literal_and_an_empty_one_stays_an_override

chunk_findings.detail: The new double-quote scanner still does not implement shell backslash escapes. Inside `"..."` it appends a backslash as an ordinary character and then processes the following character as if it were unescaped. For the valid command text `SKIP="a\\b" pre-commit run --all-files` (two backslash characters between the quotes), the shell would resolve the assignment value to `a\b`, but `_leading_skip` returns `a\\b` with `active=False`, so the surrounding `scope_to_diff` path rebuilds a single-quoted literal containing two backslashes and the CI run receives a different SKIP value. The same branch also treats `SKIP="lint\$slow" ...` as active even though `\$` is a literal `$`, causing the inherited SKIP not to be merged. This contradicts the docstring’s “value the shell would resolve it to” and the earlier requirement to merge a parseable leading SKIP with the environment’s SKIP.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The new double-quote escape handling and the unquoted backslash handling do not account for backslash-newline line continuation. In shell, an unquoted `\<newline>` removes both characters, and inside double quotes a backslash also retains special meaning before a newline (not only before `$`, backtick, `"` and `\`). Given a multi-line CI command such as `SKIP=a\` + newline + `b pre-commit run --all-files`, the shell parses the assignment value as `ab` and the command as `pre-commit ...`, but `_leading_skip` appends the newline as part of the value and returns `a\nb`; `scope_to_diff` then rebuilds a single-quoted value containing a newline, changing the command. The same corruption occurs inside double quotes, e.g. `SKIP="a\` + newline + `b" ...`, where the expected value is `ab` but the parser keeps both the backslash and the newline.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci.py:_leading_skip

chunk_findings.detail: The added double-backslash assertion only checks a prefix ending at `pre-commit run `. A returned command such as `SKIP="${SKIP:+$SKIP,}"'a\b' pre-commit run --all-files` satisfies the `startswith` assertion even though `--all-files` was not replaced by `--from-ref/--to-ref`. The test would therefore pass while the CI run still lints the whole tree, which is the failure mode the diff-scoping change is meant to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: The new implementation makes the service-layer `in_process` depend on `ddflow.surfaces` having been imported first. If a caller imports only the service module (which is allowed by the layering rule this change is trying to satisfy) and calls `in_process(["config"])`, `_parser_factory[0]` is still `None`, so the function returns `P.Captured(error=RuntimeError("no ddflow CLI parser is bound in this process ..."))` with no help output. Previously, the same call would build the parser and return the help text. The added comment claims every process/test has a factory registered, but that is true only after `ddflow.surfaces` is imported; nothing in the service layer enforces or performs that import, and the function's docstring still promises it answers without a spawn. This is a behavior regression for service-only usage, direct unit tests, or any environment where the service module is imported/reloaded without also importing `ddflow.surfaces`.
